<!-- / -->

# Mubit

> Mubit passes your app's calls on to your model provider and records them. It groups similar calls into tasks and trains adapters, small models each made for one task. Each adapter version is tested against your provider model's answers, and you can compare a passing version with your provider model in Try models.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/index.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Mubit passes your app's calls on to your model provider and records them. It groups similar calls into tasks and trains adapters, small models each made for one task. Each adapter version is tested against your provider model's answers, and you can compare a passing version with your provider model in **Try models**.

Give your client Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key:

#### OpenAI

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)
```

#### Anthropic

```python
import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic",  # no /v1
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)
```

#### Gemini

```python
import os
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client(
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
    http_options=types.HttpOptions(
        base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/gemini",  # no /v1beta
    ),
)
```

Your model IDs stay the same.

[Send your first call](/quickstart)

## How it works

1. [Connect](/quickstart): give your client Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key.
2. [See your calls](/guides/requests): each call shows in **Requests**, with its request and reply.
3. [Find tasks](/guides/tasks-and-sessions): calls with the same model, instructions, tools, tool choice and output format form a task.
4. [Train and test an adapter](/guides/first-adapter): Mubit tests each adapter version against your provider model's answers, and you can compare a passing version in **Try models**.

[Concepts](/concepts) explains each term.

## Start from

- **[Your app](/quickstart)** — Send one call with the OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini SDK, or with curl.
- **[A coding tool](/guides/coding-tools)** — Point Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Aider at Mubit.
- **[Past traces](/guides/import-past-calls)** — Import past calls from Langfuse, Braintrust or Pydantic Logfire.

## Good to know

- Calls run on your provider key, or on the starter credit where it's offered. See [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys).
- The examples use the host `https://api.mubit.ai`. Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.


---

<!-- /quickstart -->

# Quickstart

> Send one call through Mubit from your terminal, then find its request and reply in Requests.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/quickstart.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Send one call through Mubit and find its request and reply in the console.

**Before you start.** Run the example in a bash or zsh terminal on your computer or a server, not in a browser. You need Python 3.10+, Node.js 22+ or curl, and an inference key for your project. If you can't create keys or choose how calls are paid, ask an admin of your organization.

## 1. Set up in the console

Open [app.mubit.ai](https://app.mubit.ai/) and sign in. Complete the first-time setup if prompted.

On **Get started**, create a Mubit key. It gets the permission **Inference: calls this project**. Copy it when shown, then set it in the terminal where you will run the example:

```bash
export MUBIT_API_KEY='YOUR_MUBIT_KEY'
```

Under **Choose how calls are paid**, select **Use the starter credit** if it's offered, or **Add your provider key**. The console names the providers the starter credit covers; for any other provider, add its API key. See [Provider-key setup](/admin/provider-keys).

## 2. Send one call

Choose your provider and language below. The example uses Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key; keep the model ID you want to call. Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.

> **Note:** **Mubit records request and reply content by default.** Use synthetic data for this example, and keep secrets out of prompts.

#### OpenAI

On the starter credit, use a model it serves, such as `gpt-6-luna`. For other models or options, add your own OpenAI key. See [On the starter credit](/guides/model-ids#on-the-starter-credit) and [Connect with the OpenAI SDK](/guides/connect-openai).

##### Python

Create a virtual environment and install the SDK:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install openai
```

Save this as `mubit-quickstart.py`:

```python [mubit-quickstart.py]
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-6-luna",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": instructions},
        {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."},
    ],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

Run it:

```bash
python mubit-quickstart.py
```

##### TypeScript

Install the SDK and `tsx`, which runs TypeScript files:

```bash
npm install openai tsx
```

Save this as `mubit-quickstart.mts`. The `.mts` ending runs it as an ES module, which its top-level `await` needs.

```ts [mubit-quickstart.mts]
import OpenAI from "openai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
  apiKey,
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
  messages: [
    { role: "system", content: instructions },
    { role: "user", content: "I was charged twice for my October invoice." },
  ],
});
console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
```

Run it:

```bash
npx tsx mubit-quickstart.mts
```

##### curl

No install needed. Run this in the terminal where you set `MUBIT_API_KEY`:

```bash [Terminal]
curl https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}
    ]
  }'
```

#### Anthropic

On the starter credit, use a model it serves, such as `claude-haiku-4-5`. For other models or options, add your own Anthropic key. See [On the starter credit](/guides/model-ids#on-the-starter-credit) and [Connect with the Anthropic SDK](/guides/connect-anthropic).

##### Python

Create a virtual environment and install the SDK:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install anthropic
```

Save this as `mubit-quickstart.py`:

```python [mubit-quickstart.py]
import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic",  # no /v1
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-4-5",
    max_tokens=64,
    system=instructions,
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."},
    ],
)
print(message.content[0].text)
```

Run it:

```bash
python mubit-quickstart.py
```

##### TypeScript

Install the SDK and `tsx`, which runs TypeScript files:

```bash
npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk tsx
```

Save this as `mubit-quickstart.mts`. The `.mts` ending runs it as an ES module, which its top-level `await` needs.

```ts [mubit-quickstart.mts]
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new Anthropic({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic", // no /v1
  apiKey,
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";

const message = await client.messages.create({
  model: "claude-haiku-4-5",
  max_tokens: 64,
  system: instructions,
  messages: [
    { role: "user", content: "I was charged twice for my October invoice." },
  ],
});
for (const block of message.content) {
  if (block.type === "text") console.log(block.text);
}
```

Run it:

```bash
npx tsx mubit-quickstart.mts
```

##### curl

No install needed. Run this in the terminal where you set `MUBIT_API_KEY`:

```bash [Terminal]
curl https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
    "max_tokens": 64,
    "system": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}
    ]
  }'
```

#### Gemini

If the console doesn't list Gemini under the starter credit, add your Gemini key under **Provider keys** first. On the starter credit, use a model it serves, such as `gemini-3.8-flash`. See [On the starter credit](/guides/model-ids#on-the-starter-credit) and [Connect with Gemini](/guides/connect-gemini).

##### Python

Create a virtual environment and install the SDK:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install google-genai
```

Save this as `mubit-quickstart.py`:

```python [mubit-quickstart.py]
import os
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client(
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
    http_options=types.HttpOptions(
        base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/gemini",  # no /v1beta
    ),
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-3.8-flash",
    contents="I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(system_instruction=instructions),
)
print(response.text)
```

Run it:

```bash
python mubit-quickstart.py
```

##### TypeScript

Install the SDK and `tsx`, which runs TypeScript files:

```bash
npm install @google/genai tsx
```

Save this as `mubit-quickstart.mts`. The `.mts` ending runs it as an ES module, which its top-level `await` needs.

```ts [mubit-quickstart.mts]
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
  apiKey,
  httpOptions: { baseUrl: "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini" }, // no /v1beta
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";

const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
  model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
  contents: "I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
  config: { systemInstruction: instructions },
});
console.log(response.text);
```

Run it:

```bash
npx tsx mubit-quickstart.mts
```

##### curl

No install needed. Run this in the terminal where you set `MUBIT_API_KEY`:

```bash [Terminal]
curl "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:generateContent" \
  -H "x-goog-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "system_instruction": {"parts": [{"text": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."}]},
    "contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}]}]
  }'
```

## 3. Check the result

For this support message, a successful reply should classify it as `billing`; exact output can vary.

In the console, open **Requests** and select your newest call. Check its **Request**, **Reply** and **Served by** details. Only calls made through the configured client go through Mubit.

If the call fails, use its error code to [find the fix](/troubleshooting).

## Next

- **[Create your first adapter](/guides/first-adapter)** — Send examples of one task, follow its training, and compare a passing version with your provider model.

<!-- /concepts -->

# Concepts

> How Mubit groups calls into tasks and uses kept examples to train and test adapters. Requests, tasks, kept examples, adapters, and the two kinds of key.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/concepts.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Mubit groups similar calls into tasks and uses kept examples to train and test adapters.

Not every call is kept, and not every version passes. Training also depends on the task's limits and eligibility.

### The diagram in words

Mubit groups recorded calls into tasks and selects kept examples. Once enough eligible examples are available and training can run, Mubit trains and tests an adapter version. A passing version can be compared in Try models. If a version is below target, review its results and provide more useful examples.

## Four terms to know

- **Request:** One call your app sends through Mubit. Recorded calls appear in **Requests**.
- **Task:** A recurring kind of request. Calls with matching model, instructions, tools, tool choice, and output format form a task.
- **Kept example:** A call Mubit accepts for training or testing. Not every recorded call becomes a kept example.
- **Adapter:** A small model trained for one task. Each training creates a version, which Mubit tests against the provider model's answers.

Once an adapter version passes its tests, you can compare it with your provider model in **Try models**. Passing a test does not guarantee suitability for every input; review representative examples from your application.

## Two different keys

Your app uses a **Mubit key** to call Mubit. Mubit uses a **provider API key** to call the provider, either through supported starter credit or your configured provider account.

A **project** holds your calls, tasks, adapters, and keys. [Project administration](/admin/projects) is separate from this learning flow.

**Next:** [Create your first adapter](/guides/first-adapter).

For detail: [Tasks and sessions](/guides/tasks-and-sessions) · [Mubit keys](/admin/mubit-keys) · [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys).


---

<!-- /guides/first-adapter -->

# Create your first adapter

> Send examples of one task, follow its training, read each version's test result, and compare a passing version with your provider model in Try models.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/first-adapter.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Send examples of one task, follow its training, and compare a passing adapter version with your provider model.

**Before you start.** Complete the [Quickstart](/quickstart). You need your Mubit key in `MUBIT_API_KEY` and provider access. This example sends 40 calls: they use your provider account or the starter credit, and passing is not guaranteed. Training must be on for your workspace: until it is, the console shows no **Adapters** page. To ask about it, see [Get help](/troubleshooting#get-help).

## 1. Send examples of one task

Use the example below. It varies the support message while keeping the model and instructions the same as in the Quickstart.

Not every call becomes a kept example. By default, a task first trains at 25 kept examples; the count your console shows is the source of truth.

#### OpenAI

##### Python

Create a virtual environment and install the SDK:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install openai
```

Save this as `mubit-first-adapter.py`:

```python [mubit-first-adapter.py]
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)
templates = [
    "I was charged twice for my {} plan this month.",
    "The {} dashboard shows an error when I export a report.",
    "How do I change the email address on my {} account?",
    "Can I get a refund for the {} plan I cancelled yesterday?",
    "The {} mobile app closes when I open settings.",
    "I can't reset the password for my {} account.",
    "Do you offer the {} plan to charities?",
    "Where can I download last month's invoice for the {} plan?",
]
plans = ["Starter", "Team", "Business", "Enterprise", "Education"]

# 8 messages x 5 plans: 40 calls of one task.
for template in templates:
    for plan in plans:
        response = client.chat.completions.create(
            model="gpt-6-luna",
            messages=[
                {"role": "system", "content": instructions},
                {"role": "user", "content": template.format(plan)},
            ],
        )
        print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

Run it:

```bash
python mubit-first-adapter.py
```

##### TypeScript

Install the SDK and `tsx`, which runs TypeScript files:

```bash
npm install openai tsx
```

Save this as `mubit-first-adapter.mts`. The `.mts` ending runs it as an ES module, which its top-level `await` needs.

```ts [mubit-first-adapter.mts]
import OpenAI from "openai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
  apiKey,
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";
const templates = [
  "I was charged twice for my {} plan this month.",
  "The {} dashboard shows an error when I export a report.",
  "How do I change the email address on my {} account?",
  "Can I get a refund for the {} plan I cancelled yesterday?",
  "The {} mobile app closes when I open settings.",
  "I can't reset the password for my {} account.",
  "Do you offer the {} plan to charities?",
  "Where can I download last month's invoice for the {} plan?",
];
const plans = ["Starter", "Team", "Business", "Enterprise", "Education"];

// 8 messages x 5 plans: 40 calls of one task.
for (const template of templates) {
  for (const plan of plans) {
    const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
      model: "gpt-6-luna",
      messages: [
        { role: "system", content: instructions },
        { role: "user", content: template.replace("{}", plan) },
      ],
    });
    console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
  }
}
```

Run it:

```bash
npx tsx mubit-first-adapter.mts
```

##### curl

No install needed. Save this as `mubit-first-adapter.sh`. It prints each call's HTTP status.

```bash [mubit-first-adapter.sh]
templates=(
  "I was charged twice for my %s plan this month."
  "The %s dashboard shows an error when I export a report."
  "How do I change the email address on my %s account?"
  "Can I get a refund for the %s plan I cancelled yesterday?"
  "The %s mobile app closes when I open settings."
  "I can't reset the password for my %s account."
  "Do you offer the %s plan to charities?"
  "Where can I download last month's invoice for the %s plan?"
)
plans=(Starter Team Business Enterprise Education)

for template in "${templates[@]}"; do
  for plan in "${plans[@]}"; do
    message=$(printf "$template" "$plan")
    curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
      https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1/chat/completions \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
      -H "content-type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model": "gpt-6-luna", "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "'"$message"'"}]}'
  done
done
```

Run it in the terminal where you set `MUBIT_API_KEY`:

```bash
bash mubit-first-adapter.sh
```

#### Anthropic

##### Python

Create a virtual environment and install the SDK:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
```

```python [mubit-first-adapter.py]
import os

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic",  # no /v1
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)
templates = [
    "I was charged twice for my {} plan this month.",
    "The {} dashboard shows an error when I export a report.",
    "How do I change the email address on my {} account?",
    "Can I get a refund for the {} plan I cancelled yesterday?",
    "The {} mobile app closes when I open settings.",
    "I can't reset the password for my {} account.",
    "Do you offer the {} plan to charities?",
    "Where can I download last month's invoice for the {} plan?",
]
plans = ["Starter", "Team", "Business", "Enterprise", "Education"]

# 8 messages x 5 plans: 40 calls of one task.
for template in templates:
    for plan in plans:
        message = client.messages.create(
            model="claude-haiku-4-5",
            max_tokens=64,
            system=instructions,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": template.format(plan)}],
        )
        print(message.content[0].text)
```

Run it:

```bash
python mubit-first-adapter.py
```

##### TypeScript

Install the SDK and `tsx`, which runs TypeScript files:

```bash
npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk tsx
```

Save this as `mubit-first-adapter.mts`. The `.mts` ending runs it as an ES module, which its top-level `await` needs.

```ts [mubit-first-adapter.mts]
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new Anthropic({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic", // no /v1
  apiKey,
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";
const templates = [
  "I was charged twice for my {} plan this month.",
  "The {} dashboard shows an error when I export a report.",
  "How do I change the email address on my {} account?",
  "Can I get a refund for the {} plan I cancelled yesterday?",
  "The {} mobile app closes when I open settings.",
  "I can't reset the password for my {} account.",
  "Do you offer the {} plan to charities?",
  "Where can I download last month's invoice for the {} plan?",

// 8 messages x 5 plans: 40 calls of one task.
for (const template of templates) {
  for (const plan of plans) {
    const message = await client.messages.create({
      model: "claude-haiku-4-5",
      max_tokens: 64,
      system: instructions,
      messages: [{ role: "user", content: template.replace("{}", plan) }],

}
```

Run it:

#### Gemini

##### Python

Create a virtual environment and install the SDK:

```bash

pip install google-genai
```

Save this as `mubit-first-adapter.py`:

```python [mubit-first-adapter.py]
import os
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client(
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
    http_options=types.HttpOptions(
        base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/gemini",  # no /v1beta
    ),
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)
templates = [
    "I was charged twice for my {} plan this month.",
    "The {} dashboard shows an error when I export a report.",
    "How do I change the email address on my {} account?",
    "Can I get a refund for the {} plan I cancelled yesterday?",
    "The {} mobile app closes when I open settings.",
    "I can't reset the password for my {} account.",
    "Do you offer the {} plan to charities?",
    "Where can I download last month's invoice for the {} plan?",
]
plans = ["Starter", "Team", "Business", "Enterprise", "Education"]

# 8 messages x 5 plans: 40 calls of one task.
for template in templates:
    for plan in plans:
        response = client.models.generate_content(
            model="gemini-3.8-flash",
            contents=template.format(plan),
            config=types.GenerateContentConfig(system_instruction=instructions),
        )
        print(response.text)
```

Run it:

```bash
python mubit-first-adapter.py
```

##### TypeScript

Install the SDK and `tsx`, which runs TypeScript files:

```bash
npm install @google/genai tsx
```

Save this as `mubit-first-adapter.mts`. The `.mts` ending runs it as an ES module, which its top-level `await` needs.

```ts [mubit-first-adapter.mts]
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
  apiKey,
  httpOptions: { baseUrl: "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini" }, // no /v1beta
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";
const templates = [
  "I was charged twice for my {} plan this month.",
  "The {} dashboard shows an error when I export a report.",
  "How do I change the email address on my {} account?",
  "Can I get a refund for the {} plan I cancelled yesterday?",
  "The {} mobile app closes when I open settings.",
  "I can't reset the password for my {} account.",
  "Do you offer the {} plan to charities?",
  "Where can I download last month's invoice for the {} plan?",
];
const plans = ["Starter", "Team", "Business", "Enterprise", "Education"];

// 8 messages x 5 plans: 40 calls of one task.
for (const template of templates) {
  for (const plan of plans) {
    const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
      model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
      contents: template.replace("{}", plan),
      config: { systemInstruction: instructions },
    });
    console.log(response.text);
  }
}
```

Run it:

```bash
npx tsx mubit-first-adapter.mts
```

##### curl

No install needed. Save this as `mubit-first-adapter.sh`. It prints each call's HTTP status.

```bash [mubit-first-adapter.sh]
templates=(
  "I was charged twice for my %s plan this month."
  "The %s dashboard shows an error when I export a report."
  "How do I change the email address on my %s account?"
  "Can I get a refund for the %s plan I cancelled yesterday?"
  "The %s mobile app closes when I open settings."
  "I can't reset the password for my %s account."
  "Do you offer the %s plan to charities?"
  "Where can I download last month's invoice for the %s plan?"
)
plans=(Starter Team Business Enterprise Education)

for template in "${templates[@]}"; do
  for plan in "${plans[@]}"; do
    message=$(printf "$template" "$plan")
    curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
      "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:generateContent" \
      -H "x-goog-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
      -H "content-type: application/json" \
      -d '{"system_instruction": {"parts": [{"text": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."}]},
        "contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "'"$message"'"}]}]}'
  done
done
```

Run it in the terminal where you set `MUBIT_API_KEY`:

```bash
bash mubit-first-adapter.sh
```

## 2. Follow the task

Open **Tasks** and find the task created from these calls. Its name comes from the first words of the instructions. Watch its status, `Collecting examples` at first, and its kept-example count, such as `12 of 25 examples`.

If it needs more examples, send new messages for the same task. When it has enough and can train, Mubit reviews the examples, trains an adapter version and tests it: the status reads `Reviewing examples`, `Training`, then `Testing`.

If progress stops, open the task and read the reason. [Why a task is waiting or cannot train](#waits-and-recovery) explains waits and failed training.

## 3. Check the result

Open **Adapters**, select the adapter, and open **History**. A `Passed` result makes that version available for comparison. `Below target` means its answers did not meet the required test result.

Read the result details before you decide what to add or change. A test result measures this version on its test cases; it does not guarantee every future answer. [What each test result means](#test-results) lists every result and what to do.

## 4. Compare with your provider

For a passing version, select **Compare with your provider**. **Try models** opens with **Side by side** on. Enter only the message, as your app's users would write it: Try models adds the task's instructions. Then select **Send to both**.

Compare the provider model's reply, on the left, with your adapter's, on the right. Try models marks its calls `not stored · trains nothing`: they don't appear in **Requests** and don't train adapters. The first start of an adapter can take a few minutes.

If no version has passed, go back to [What each test result means](#test-results). If the adapter isn't in Try models, see [Why an adapter is unavailable in Try models](#try-models-unavailable).

To follow your requests, tasks and adapters over time, open **Overview** in the console.

## Results and recovery

### What each test result means

Each version gets one test result: `Passed`, `Below target`, `Malformed tool calls`, `Prompt only` or `Not tested`. Select the adapter, then open **History**. Each version's row shows its test result:

| Result | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Passed` | The version answers close enough to your provider model. On **Overview**, the adapter's line reads `v1 passed its tests`. | [Compare it in Try models](#4-compare-with-your-provider). |
| `Below target` | The version answers less like your provider model than it needs to. The line says by how much, such as `Matched {a}% of your provider model's answers on {n} test cases · needs {need}%`, or `Passed {a}% of {n} required test cases · needs 100%`. | Send more calls of the task. See [After a version that didn't pass](#after-a-version-that-didnt-pass). |
| `Malformed tool calls` | Some of the version's tool calls were malformed: `{k} of {n} tool calls were malformed · needs 0`. | Send more calls of the task. |
| `Prompt only` | The base model, the open model the adapter is built on, did as well as the adapter when given the task's prompt. | A prompt-only version can't be tried in Try models. Send more calls of the task for a new version. |
| `Not tested` | The version has no test result. When Mubit gives a reason, it shows when you point at the result. | Send more calls of the task for a new version. |

While Mubit grades a version, the adapter's line reads `Waiting for grading on {k} test cases`. While the newest version is below its target, the adapter's card reads `Not ready yet`.

### Why a task is waiting or cannot train

#### Waits

A task can wait before it trains. Point at its status on **Tasks** to see the wait, or open the task: its page says it in words.

| Wait | Why | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Waiting: today's training limit` | Today's training limit is reached. It resets at 00:00 UTC. | Nothing. Training starts after the reset. |
| `Waiting: the pause between trainings` | Mubit pauses between two trainings. | Nothing. Training starts after the pause. |
| `Waiting for more examples: {k} of {need}` | The task has too few examples to keep some back as test cases. | Send more calls with new messages. |
| `Waiting for new examples` | A training failed. Mubit tries again when new examples arrive. It does not retry the same ones. | Send more calls with new messages. |

#### Can't train

When a task's first training fails, its status reads `Can't train`, and the task's page reads `No adapter yet:` and the reason:

| Reason | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `too few examples to train on` | Send more calls with new messages. |
| `examples too long to train on` | Send calls with shorter requests and answers. |
| `the training run failed` | Send more calls with new messages. |
| `the first training stopped` | Send more calls with new messages. |

There is no button that retries a training. After a failed training, Mubit tries again only when new examples arrive, so recovery means sending new calls of the task.

#### After a version that didn't pass

Under a version that didn't pass, the adapter shows what happens next:

- `Next: a new version after {need} new examples`: the task trains a new version once that many new examples arrive. Send more calls of the task.
- `Next: retraining paused: {reason}`: the reason says why the task doesn't retrain now.

A version whose training failed reads `Training failed`.

### Why an adapter is unavailable in Try models

Try models runs provider models on Mubit's key. Your organization has a number of Try models calls each day: the page shows how many are left, and the count resets at 00:00 UTC.

| What you see | Why | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No **Compare with your provider** on the adapter | No version of the adapter has passed its tests. | Follow the task until a version passes. See [What each test result means](#test-results). |
| `Not in Try models: prompt only` | The version's result is `Prompt only`: the base model with the task's prompt did as well as the adapter. | Send more calls of the task for a new version. |
| `Not in Try models yet` | Try models can't run adapters in this workspace yet. | Nothing to do in the console. To ask about it, see [Get help](/troubleshooting#get-help). |
| `Not in Try models: its base model isn't served here` | Try models doesn't serve the base model this adapter is built on. | Nothing to do in the console. To ask about it, see [Get help](/troubleshooting#get-help). |
| `Try models is off` | Try models is not switched on for this workspace. | Nothing to do in the console. To ask about it, see [Get help](/troubleshooting#get-help). |
| `Your organization has used today's Try models calls. Try again after 00:00 UTC.` | Your organization has used its Try models calls for the day. | Wait until 00:00 UTC. |
| `Try models has reached today's limit for this workspace. Try again after 00:00 UTC.` | The workspace has reached its Try models limit for the day. | Wait until 00:00 UTC. |
| `Starting your adapter. The first try takes a few minutes. Keep this page open.` | The adapter is starting. | Keep the page open: it sends your message again every 15 s, for up to 20 minutes. |
| `Your adapter didn't start. Try again later, or choose a provider model.` | The adapter didn't start, or your organization has used its 3 adapter starts for this UTC day. | Try again later, or choose a provider model. |

## Next

- **[Understand tasks and sessions](/guides/tasks-and-sessions)** — What makes a task, and how to group a conversation's calls into one session.

# Connect with the OpenAI SDK

> Point the OpenAI SDK at Mubit with a new base URL and your Mubit key, send a call, stream an answer, and find the call in Requests.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/connect-openai.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

In an SDK, update where you create your client: give it Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key. With curl, change the URL and the key in its header. Keep your model IDs and the rest of your code.

## Base URL

The base URL is `https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1`. It ends in `/v1`, as the OpenAI SDK expects.

Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.

## Key

Pass your Mubit key as the SDK's API key. The SDK sends it in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.

The examples read the key from `MUBIT_API_KEY`. To create a key and set it, follow [step 1 of the Quickstart](/quickstart#1-set-up-in-the-console).

## Send a call

Install the SDK: `pip install openai` for Python, or `npm install openai` for TypeScript.

```python [Python]
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-6-luna",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": instructions},
        {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."},
    ],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import OpenAI from "openai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
  apiKey,
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
  messages: [
    { role: "system", content: instructions },
    { role: "user", content: "I was charged twice for my October invoice." },
  ],
});
console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
```

```bash [curl]
curl https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}
    ]
  }'
```

The TypeScript examples use top-level `await`, so run them as ES modules: save the file as `openai.mts` and run `npx tsx openai.mts`, or add `"type": "module"` to your `package.json`.

Chat Completions and Responses both work through the same base URL.

## Stream the answer

Set `stream` to true. Mubit streams the answer back to your app.

```python [Python]
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-6-luna",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "Reply to the support message in two short sentences."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."},
    ],
    stream=True,
)
for chunk in stream:
    if chunk.choices and chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
        print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end="", flush=True)
print()
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import OpenAI from "openai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
  apiKey,
});

const stream = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
  messages: [
    { role: "system", content: "Reply to the support message in two short sentences." },
    { role: "user", content: "I was charged twice for my October invoice." },
  ],
  stream: true,
});
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.choices[0]?.delta?.content ?? "");
}
process.stdout.write("\n");
```

```bash [curl]
curl -N https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Reply to the support message in two short sentences."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}
    ]
  }'
```

`curl -N` prints each event as it arrives.

## Or set the SDK's environment variables

The OpenAI SDK reads its base URL and key from the environment when your code doesn't pass them. To point an app at Mubit without a code change, set these two variables where it runs:

```bash
export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1
export OPENAI_API_KEY="$MUBIT_API_KEY"
```

## See the call in Requests

1. In the console, open **Requests**.
2. Find your call at the top. The list is newest first.
3. Check **Model asked**. It shows the model ID your app sent.
4. Select the row. The call opens with its **Request** and its **Reply**.

A streamed call shows its whole reply.

## What Mubit forwards and trains on

- **Forwarded:** when Mubit sends a call on to OpenAI, it sends your request with your OpenAI key, or the starter credit's key, in place of your Mubit key. It doesn't pass on cookies, `x-middleware-store` or `x-middleware-record`. On the starter credit, some models, paths and options are refused: see [Starter credit errors](/troubleshooting#starter-credit-errors).
- **Trained on:** adapters train only on kept examples: the recorded calls Mubit accepts for a task. A call recorded without its request and reply is never a kept example.

## Frameworks and coding tools

[Frameworks](/guides/frameworks) covers the Vercel AI SDK, LangChain and the OpenAI Agents SDK, and [Coding tools](/guides/coding-tools) covers Codex and Aider. Turn the Agents SDK's tracing off first, as Frameworks shows: with it on, the SDK can send your Mubit key to OpenAI.

## If a call fails

The error names its code. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting) lists the codes and what to do. Each answer carries the call's ID in the `x-middleware-request-id` header: see [Find a call's request ID](/guides/requests#find-a-calls-request-id).

## Next

- [Keep your model IDs](/guides/model-ids)
- [Tasks and sessions](/guides/tasks-and-sessions)
- [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys)

# Connect with the Anthropic SDK

> Point the Anthropic SDK at Mubit with a new base URL and your Mubit key, send a call, stream an answer, and find the call in Requests.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/connect-anthropic.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

In an SDK, update where you create your client: give it Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key. With curl, change the URL and the key in its header. Keep your model IDs and the rest of your code.

## Base URL

The base URL is `https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic`. Leave `/v1` off the end: the Anthropic SDK adds it.

Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.

## Key

Pass your Mubit key as the SDK's API key. The SDK sends it in the `x-api-key` header. Mubit also reads it from `Authorization: Bearer`.

The examples read the key from `MUBIT_API_KEY`. To create a key and set it, follow [step 1 of the Quickstart](/quickstart#1-set-up-in-the-console).

> **Note:** Send your Mubit key only. If `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` holds another credential, the Anthropic SDKs can send it beside your key, and Mubit refuses the call with a `401`. Unset it, or set it to your Mubit key.

## Send a call

Install the SDK: `pip install anthropic` for Python, or `npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk` for TypeScript.

```python [Python]
import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic",  # no /v1
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-4-5",
    max_tokens=64,
    system=instructions,
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."},
    ],
)
print(message.content[0].text)
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new Anthropic({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic", // no /v1
  apiKey,
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";

const message = await client.messages.create({
  model: "claude-haiku-4-5",
  max_tokens: 64,
  system: instructions,
  messages: [
    { role: "user", content: "I was charged twice for my October invoice." },
  ],
});
for (const block of message.content) {
  if (block.type === "text") console.log(block.text);
}
```

```bash [curl]
curl https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
    "max_tokens": 64,
    "system": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}
    ]
  }'
```

The TypeScript examples use top-level `await`, so run them as ES modules: save the file as `anthropic.mts` and run `npx tsx anthropic.mts`, or add `"type": "module"` to your `package.json`.

## Stream the answer

Use the SDK's `stream` helper, or set `stream` to true. Mubit streams the answer back to your app.

```python [Python]
import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic",  # no /v1
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

with client.messages.stream(
    model="claude-haiku-4-5",
    max_tokens=256,
    system="Reply to the support message in two short sentences.",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."},
    ],
) as stream:
    for text in stream.text_stream:
        print(text, end="", flush=True)
print()
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new Anthropic({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic", // no /v1
  apiKey,
});

const stream = client.messages.stream({
  model: "claude-haiku-4-5",
  max_tokens: 256,
  system: "Reply to the support message in two short sentences.",
  messages: [
    { role: "user", content: "I was charged twice for my October invoice." },
  ],
});
stream.on("text", (text) => process.stdout.write(text));
await stream.finalMessage();
process.stdout.write("\n");
```

```bash [curl]
curl -N https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "stream": true,
    "system": "Reply to the support message in two short sentences.",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}
    ]
  }'
```

`curl -N` prints each event as it arrives.

## Or set the SDK's environment variables

The Anthropic SDK reads its base URL and key from the environment when your code doesn't pass them. To point an app at Mubit without a code change, set these two variables where it runs:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$MUBIT_API_KEY"
unset ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
```

The SDKs can send `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` beside the key, so the last line unsets it. Another credential left there would make Mubit refuse the call.

## See the call in Requests

1. In the console, open **Requests**.
2. Find your call at the top. The list is newest first.
3. Check **Model asked**. It shows the model ID your app sent.
4. Select the row. The call opens with its **Request** and its **Reply**.

A streamed call shows its whole reply.

## What Mubit forwards and trains on

- **Forwarded:** when Mubit sends a call on to Anthropic, it sends your request with your Anthropic key, or the starter credit's key, in place of your Mubit key. Headers such as `anthropic-version` and `anthropic-beta` go on as you sent them. Cookies, `x-middleware-store` and `x-middleware-record` don't. On the starter credit, some models, paths and options are refused: see [Starter credit errors](/troubleshooting#starter-credit-errors).
- **Trained on:** adapters train only on kept examples: the recorded calls Mubit accepts for a task. A call recorded without its request and reply is never a kept example.

## Frameworks and coding tools

[Frameworks](/guides/frameworks) covers the Vercel AI SDK and LangChain, and [Coding tools](/guides/coding-tools) covers Claude Code.

## If a call fails

The error names its code. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting) lists the codes and what to do. Each answer carries the call's ID in the `x-middleware-request-id` header: see [Find a call's request ID](/guides/requests#find-a-calls-request-id).

<!-- /guides/connect-gemini -->

# Connect with Gemini

> Point the Google Gen AI SDK at Mubit with a new base URL and your Mubit key, send a call, stream an answer, and find the call in Requests.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/connect-gemini.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

In an SDK, update where you create your client: give it Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key. With curl, change the URL and the key in its header. Keep your model IDs and the rest of your code.

> **Note:** If the console doesn't list Gemini under the starter credit, add your Gemini key under **Provider keys** first, as the [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys) page shows.

## Base URL

The base URL is `https://api.mubit.ai/gemini`. Leave the version path off the end: the SDK adds `/v1beta`.

Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.

## Key

Pass your Mubit key as the SDK's API key. The SDK sends it in the `x-goog-api-key` header. If you call the API without the SDK, send the key in `x-goog-api-key` too, not in `?key=`.

The examples read the key from `MUBIT_API_KEY`. To create a key and set it, follow [step 1 of the Quickstart](/quickstart#1-set-up-in-the-console).

## Send a call

Install the SDK: `pip install google-genai` for Python, or `npm install @google/genai` for TypeScript.

```python [Python]
import os
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client(
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
    http_options=types.HttpOptions(
        base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/gemini",  # no /v1beta
    ),
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-3.8-flash",
    contents="I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(system_instruction=instructions),
)
print(response.text)
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
  apiKey,
  httpOptions: { baseUrl: "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini" }, // no /v1beta
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";

const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
  model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
  contents: "I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
  config: { systemInstruction: instructions },
});
console.log(response.text);
```

```bash [curl]
curl "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:generateContent" \
  -H "x-goog-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "system_instruction": {"parts": [{"text": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."}]},
    "contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}]}]
  }'
```

The TypeScript examples use top-level `await`, so run them as ES modules: save the file as `gemini.mts` and run `npx tsx gemini.mts`, or add `"type": "module"` to your `package.json`.

If the call answers `403 provider_key_missing`, your project has no Gemini key yet.

## Stream the answer

Use the SDK's stream method, or call `:streamGenerateContent`. Mubit streams the answer back to your app.

```python [Python]
import os
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client(
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
    http_options=types.HttpOptions(
        base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/gemini",  # no /v1beta
    ),
)

for chunk in client.models.generate_content_stream(
    model="gemini-3.8-flash",
    contents="I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        system_instruction="Reply to the support message in two short sentences.",
    ),
):
    print(chunk.text or "", end="", flush=True)
print()
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
  apiKey,
  httpOptions: { baseUrl: "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini" }, // no /v1beta
});

const stream = await ai.models.generateContentStream({
  model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
  contents: "I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
  config: { systemInstruction: "Reply to the support message in two short sentences." },
});
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.text ?? "");
}
process.stdout.write("\n");
```

```bash [curl]
curl -N "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse" \
  -H "x-goog-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "system_instruction": {"parts": [{"text": "Reply to the support message in two short sentences."}]},
    "contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}]}]
  }'
```

With `?alt=sse`, the answer comes as server-sent events. `curl -N` prints each event as it arrives.

## Or set the SDK's environment variables

The Gemini SDKs read their base URL and key from the environment when your code doesn't pass them. To point an app at Mubit without a code change, run these lines in the shell where the app runs:

```bash
export GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=https://api.mubit.ai/gemini
export GEMINI_API_KEY="$MUBIT_API_KEY"
unset GOOGLE_API_KEY
```

The SDKs use `GOOGLE_API_KEY` before `GEMINI_API_KEY`, so the last line unsets it. A Google key left in the shell would go out in place of your Mubit key.

## See the call in Requests

1. In the console, open **Requests**.
2. Find your call at the top. The list is newest first.
3. Check **Model asked**. It shows the model ID from your call.
4. Select the row. The call opens with its **Request** and its **Reply**.

A streamed call shows its whole reply.

## What Mubit forwards and trains on

- **Forwarded:** when Mubit sends a call on to Gemini, it sends your request with your Gemini key, or the starter credit's key, in place of your Mubit key. It doesn't pass on cookies, `x-middleware-store` or `x-middleware-record`.
- **Trained on:** adapters train only on kept examples: the recorded calls Mubit accepts for a task. A call recorded without its request and reply is never a kept example.

## Frameworks and coding tools

[Frameworks](/guides/frameworks) covers the Vercel AI SDK, and [Coding tools](/guides/coding-tools) covers Gemini CLI. To call Gemini through the OpenAI SDK, use the base URL `https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta/openai`. On the starter credit, this base URL gets `403 starter_credit_route`: add your own Gemini key to use it.

## If a call fails

The error names its code. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting) lists the codes and what to do. Each answer carries the call's ID in the `x-middleware-request-id` header: see [Find a call's request ID](/guides/requests#find-a-calls-request-id).

## Next

- [Keep your model IDs](/guides/model-ids)
- [Tasks and sessions](/guides/tasks-and-sessions)
- [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys)

# Connect with plain HTTP

> The paths, keys and headers of the Mubit API for apps that call it without an SDK.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/connect-http.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Mubit takes each provider's own requests. Send the request you send today to Mubit's host, under the provider's prefix, with your Mubit key in place of the provider key.

The [API reference](/reference/api) has all of it in one place, with limits, retries and sizes.

## Host

The host is `https://api.mubit.ai`. Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.

## Paths

Each provider has a prefix. After it, use the provider's own path.

| Provider | Prefix | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `/openai/v1` | `POST /openai/v1/chat/completions`, `POST /openai/v1/responses`, `POST /openai/v1/embeddings`, `GET /openai/v1/models` |
| Anthropic | `/anthropic` | `POST /anthropic/v1/messages`, `POST /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens`, `GET /anthropic/v1/models` |
| Gemini | `/gemini` | `POST /gemini/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`, `POST /gemini/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`, `GET /gemini/v1beta/models` |
| OpenAI-compatible services | `/compat/{service}/v1` | `POST /compat/openrouter/v1/chat/completions` |

For OpenAI-compatible services, see [OpenAI-compatible services](/guides/openai-compatible). For the base URL each SDK takes, see [Paths](/reference/api#paths) in the API reference.

A path outside these prefixes gets `404 unknown_route`. Organization and admin endpoints are not available through Mubit: they get `403 admin_path_refused`.

> **Note:** The starter credit serves fewer paths. After the prefix: on Anthropic, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/messages/count_tokens` and `/v1/models`; on OpenAI, `/chat/completions`, `/responses`, `/embeddings` and `/models`; on Gemini, `/{version}/models/{model}:generateContent` and `:streamGenerateContent`, where `{version}` is a version such as `v1beta` or `v1`; on an OpenAI-compatible service, `/chat/completions` and `/models`. Any other path gets `403 starter_credit_route` until you add your own key for that provider. The starter credit covers only the providers the console names.

## Key

Send your Mubit key in the header your provider uses for its key:

| Provider | Header |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible services | `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MUBIT_KEY` |
| Anthropic | `x-api-key: YOUR_MUBIT_KEY`, or `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MUBIT_KEY` |
| Gemini | `x-goog-api-key: YOUR_MUBIT_KEY` |

Send one key, and only your Mubit key. Mubit refuses a call that carries a provider key, a sign-in token, or a second, different key, with a `401`. For Gemini, send the key in the header, not in `?key=`.

## Examples

Each example sends one support message and prints the answer with its headers (`-i`).

```bash [OpenAI]
curl -i https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "The export button on my dashboard shows an error."}
    ]
  }'
```

```bash [Anthropic]
curl -i https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
    "max_tokens": 64,
    "system": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "The export button on my dashboard shows an error."}
    ]
  }'
```

```bash [Gemini]
curl -i "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:generateContent" \
  -H "x-goog-api-key: $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "system_instruction": {"parts": [{"text": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."}]},
    "contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "The export button on my dashboard shows an error."}]}]
  }'
```

The examples read your key from `MUBIT_API_KEY`. To stream, see the page for your provider: [OpenAI](/guides/connect-openai#stream-the-answer), [Anthropic](/guides/connect-anthropic#stream-the-answer) or [Gemini](/guides/connect-gemini#stream-the-answer).

## Headers

Mubit passes most other headers to the provider as you sent them, such as `anthropic-version` and `anthropic-beta`. It doesn't pass on cookies.

Mubit reads these optional headers, and doesn't send them to the provider:

| Header | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `x-middleware-store` | `false` keeps the call's request and answer out of Mubit's record. |
| `x-middleware-record` | `full`, `metadata` or `off`: how much of the call Mubit keeps. |

Every answer carries the header `x-middleware-request-id`: the call's ID in Mubit. [Response headers](/reference/api#response-headers) lists the headers Mubit sends back.

## What Mubit forwards and trains on

- **Forwarded:** when Mubit sends a call on to a provider, it sends your request with that provider's key, or the starter credit's key, in place of your Mubit key. Other headers go on as [Headers](#headers) lists. On the starter credit, some models, paths and options are refused: see [Starter credit errors](/troubleshooting#starter-credit-errors).
- **Trained on:** adapters train only on kept examples: the recorded calls Mubit accepts for a task. A call recorded without its request and reply is never a kept example.

## Answers and errors

Mubit passes your provider's answers back to your app, its errors included.

Mubit's own errors use your provider's error format. Their `type` is `middleware_gateway_error`, and they name a `code`, such as `missing_key` or `unknown_route`. In Gemini's format, both are in the error's `ErrorInfo` detail: the code is its `reason`, and the type is in its `metadata`. For example, a call to OpenAI's path with no key gets:

```json
{"error":{"code":"missing_key","message":"No API key was provided. Send your Mubit key where the provider's SDK sends its API key.","param":null,"request_id":"mreq_…","type":"middleware_gateway_error"}}
```

The [API reference](/reference/api#errors) shows the format for each provider, and [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting#mubits-errors) lists the codes and what to do.

<!-- /guides/openai-compatible -->

# OpenAI-compatible services

> Call OpenRouter, Groq, Together or Mistral through Mubit with the OpenAI SDK, using your own key for the service or the starter credit where the console lists it.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/openai-compatible.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Mubit takes calls for four services that speak the OpenAI API: OpenRouter, Groq, Together and Mistral. Use the OpenAI SDK, or plain HTTP, with the service's base URL under Mubit.

## Before you start

Add your key for the service, unless the console lists that service among the providers the starter credit covers.

1. In the sidebar, under **Workspace**, open **Provider keys**.
2. Select **Add key**.
3. Under **Provider**, choose **OpenAI-compatible**.
4. Under **Service**, choose the service.
5. Paste the service's key in **API key**.
6. Select **Check and save**.

## Base URL

Each service has its own base URL. The service's name is part of the path, and the base URL ends in `/v1`.

| Service | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| OpenRouter | `https://api.mubit.ai/compat/openrouter/v1` |
| Groq | `https://api.mubit.ai/compat/groq/v1` |
| Together | `https://api.mubit.ai/compat/together/v1` |
| Mistral | `https://api.mubit.ai/compat/mistral/v1` |

Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows. It shows these on its **OpenAI-compatible** line: choose the service under **Service**.

## Send a call

Pass your Mubit key as the API key. The examples use OpenRouter and read the key from `MUBIT_API_KEY`. Replace `MODEL_ID` with a model ID of the service, as the service names it.

```python [Python]
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/compat/openrouter/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="MODEL_ID",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": instructions},
        {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."},
    ],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import OpenAI from "openai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/compat/openrouter/v1",
  apiKey,
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "MODEL_ID",
  messages: [
    { role: "system", content: instructions },
    { role: "user", content: "I was charged twice for my October invoice." },
  ],
});
console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
```

```bash [curl]
curl https://api.mubit.ai/compat/openrouter/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "MODEL_ID",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my October invoice."}
    ]
  }'
```

The TypeScript example uses top-level `await`, so run it as an ES module: save the file as `compat.mts` and run `npx tsx compat.mts`, or add `"type": "module"` to your `package.json`.

For another service, change `openrouter` in the base URL to `groq`, `together` or `mistral`.

## What these base URLs serve

These paths: `POST /chat/completions`, `POST /embeddings`, `GET /models` and `GET /models/{id}`. Any other path or method gets `404 unknown_route`. A service name that isn't in the table gets `404 unknown_provider`, and the message lists the services.

If you have no key saved for the service and the starter credit doesn't cover it, the call gets `403 provider_key_missing`.

## See the call in Requests

1. In the console, open **Requests**.
2. Find your call at the top. The list is newest first.
3. Check **Model asked**. It shows the model ID your app sent.

## What Mubit forwards and trains on

- **Forwarded:** when Mubit sends a call on to the service, it sends your request with your key for that service, or the starter credit's key where the console lists that service under the starter credit, in place of your Mubit key. It doesn't pass on cookies, `x-middleware-store` or `x-middleware-record`.
- **Trained on:** adapters train only on kept examples: the recorded calls Mubit accepts for a task. A call recorded without its request and reply is never a kept example.

## Frameworks and coding tools

[Coding tools](/guides/coding-tools#aider) shows Aider with a service's base URL.

## If a call fails

The error names its code. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting) lists the codes and what to do.

# Frameworks

> Point the Vercel AI SDK, LangChain and the OpenAI Agents SDK at Mubit with Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/frameworks.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Each framework on this page speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini API. To point one at Mubit, give it Mubit's base URL for that provider and your Mubit key. Keep your model IDs and the rest of your code.

Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.

The examples read the key from `MUBIT_API_KEY`. To create a key and set it, follow [step 1 of the Quickstart](/quickstart#1-set-up-in-the-console).

## Vercel AI SDK

Install the SDK and the provider packages you use: `npm install ai @ai-sdk/openai @ai-sdk/anthropic @ai-sdk/google`.

Each provider package takes a `baseURL`. The AI SDK expects the version path at the end of each one, Anthropic's and Gemini's included:

| Provider | `baseURL` |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1` |
| Anthropic | `https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic/v1` |
| Gemini | `https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta` |

### OpenAI

```ts
import { createOpenAI } from "@ai-sdk/openai";
import { generateText } from "ai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const openai = createOpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
  apiKey,
});

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: openai("gpt-6-luna"),
  system:
    "Sort the support message into one category: " +
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
  prompt: "I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
});
console.log(text);
```

`openai("…")` calls the Responses API. For Chat Completions, use `openai.chat("…")`. Both work through the same base URL.

### Anthropic

```ts
import { createAnthropic } from "@ai-sdk/anthropic";
import { generateText } from "ai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const anthropic = createAnthropic({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic/v1",
  apiKey,
});

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: anthropic("claude-haiku-4-5"),
  system:
    "Sort the support message into one category: " +
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
  prompt: "I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
});
console.log(text);
```

### Gemini

> **Note:** If the console doesn't list Gemini under the starter credit, add your Gemini key under **Provider keys** first, as the [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys) page shows.

```ts
import { createGoogleGenerativeAI } from "@ai-sdk/google";
import { generateText } from "ai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const google = createGoogleGenerativeAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta",
  apiKey,
});

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: google("gemini-3.8-flash"),
  system:
    "Sort the support message into one category: " +
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
  prompt: "I was charged twice for my October invoice.",
});
console.log(text);
```

The examples use top-level `await`, so run them as ES modules: give the file an `.mts` name, for example `vercel-openai.mts`, and run `npx tsx vercel-openai.mts`, or add `"type": "module"` to your `package.json`.

Tested with `ai` 7.0.148, `@ai-sdk/openai` 4.0.99, `@ai-sdk/anthropic` 4.0.85 and `@ai-sdk/google` 4.0.102.

## LangChain

Install the packages you use: `pip install langchain-openai langchain-anthropic` for Python, or `npm install @langchain/openai @langchain/anthropic @langchain/core` for TypeScript.

### ChatOpenAI

Give `ChatOpenAI` the OpenAI base URL, which ends in `/v1`. In Python it's `base_url`; in TypeScript it goes under `configuration`.

```python [Python]
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(
    model="gpt-6-luna",
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

reply = llm.invoke([
    ("system", "Sort the support message into one category: "
               "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."),
    ("human", "I was charged twice for my October invoice."),
])
print(reply.content)
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import { ChatOpenAI } from "@langchain/openai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const llm = new ChatOpenAI({
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
  apiKey,
  configuration: { baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1" },
});

const reply = await llm.invoke([
  [
    "system",
    "Sort the support message into one category: " +
      "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
  ],
  ["human", "I was charged twice for my October invoice."],
]);
console.log(reply.content);
```

### ChatAnthropic

Give `ChatAnthropic` the Anthropic base URL. Leave `/v1` off the end: the Anthropic SDK underneath adds it. In Python it's `base_url`; in TypeScript it's `anthropicApiUrl`.

> **Note:** Send your Mubit key only. If `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` holds another credential, the TypeScript `ChatAnthropic` sends it beside your key, and Mubit refuses the call with a `401`. Unset it, or set it to your Mubit key.

```python [Python]
import os
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic

llm = ChatAnthropic(
    model="claude-haiku-4-5",
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

reply = llm.invoke([
    ("system", "Sort the support message into one category: "
               "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."),
    ("human", "I was charged twice for my October invoice."),
])
print(reply.content)
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import { ChatAnthropic } from "@langchain/anthropic";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const llm = new ChatAnthropic({
  model: "claude-haiku-4-5",
  apiKey,
  anthropicApiUrl: "https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic",
});

const reply = await llm.invoke([
  [
    "system",
    "Sort the support message into one category: " +
      "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
  ],
  ["human", "I was charged twice for my October invoice."],
]);
console.log(reply.content);
```

LangChain also reads the SDKs' environment variables. With `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` set as [the OpenAI page](/guides/connect-openai#or-set-the-sdks-environment-variables) shows, or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as [the Anthropic page](/guides/connect-anthropic#or-set-the-sdks-environment-variables) shows, leave out the base URL and the key.

Run the TypeScript examples as ES modules, as for the AI SDK above.

Tested with `langchain-openai` 1.7.2 and `langchain-anthropic` 1.7.6 for Python, and `@langchain/openai` 1.6.3, `@langchain/anthropic` 1.5.13 and `@langchain/core` 1.2.20 for TypeScript.

## OpenAI Agents SDK

> **Warning:** Turn the SDK's tracing off before anything else. With tracing on, the SDK uploads each run's trace, prompts and replies included, to OpenAI directly. The Python SDK signs it with the key of the client you give it, which is your Mubit key. The TypeScript SDK uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`, which holds your Mubit key if you set it as [the OpenAI page](/guides/connect-openai#or-set-the-sdks-environment-variables) shows. Each example below turns tracing off in its first lines.

Install the SDK: `pip install openai-agents` for Python, or `npm install @openai/agents openai zod` for TypeScript.

Give the SDK an OpenAI client with the OpenAI base URL and your Mubit key, and make it the default client:

```python [Python]
import os
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from agents import Agent, Runner, set_default_openai_client, set_tracing_disabled

# Before anything else: with tracing on, the SDK sends your Mubit key to OpenAI.
set_tracing_disabled(True)

set_default_openai_client(
    AsyncOpenAI(
        base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
        api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
    )
)

agent = Agent(
    name="Support triage",
    instructions="Sort the support message into one category: "
                 "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
    model="gpt-6-luna",
)

result = Runner.run_sync(agent, "I was charged twice for my October invoice.")
print(result.final_output)
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import OpenAI from "openai";
import { Agent, run, setDefaultOpenAIClient, setTracingDisabled } from "@openai/agents";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

// Before anything else: with tracing on, the SDK uploads traces to OpenAI directly.
setTracingDisabled(true);

setDefaultOpenAIClient(
  new OpenAI({
    baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
    apiKey,
  }),
);

const agent = new Agent({
  name: "Support triage",
  instructions:
    "Sort the support message into one category: " +
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.",
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
});

const result = await run(agent, "I was charged twice for my October invoice.");
console.log(result.finalOutput);
```

The SDK calls the Responses API. Mubit takes it on the same base URL. Run the TypeScript example as an ES module, as for the AI SDK above.

Tested with `openai-agents` 0.24.0 and `openai` 3.36.0 for Python, and `@openai/agents` 0.21.0 and `openai` 7.41.0 for TypeScript.

## See the calls in Requests

Each call shows in **Requests** like any other: open it in the console and find the call at the top. **Model asked** shows the model ID your app sent.

## If a call fails

The error names its code. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting) lists the codes and what to do.

## Next

- [Coding tools](/guides/coding-tools)
- [Keep your model IDs](/guides/model-ids)
- [Tasks and sessions](/guides/tasks-and-sessions)
