<!-- /guides/claude-code -->

# Use Claude Code with Mubit

> Send Claude Code's calls through Mubit. Add your Anthropic key and create a Mubit key in the console, set five environment variables, and check the first call in Requests.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/claude-code.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Claude Code reads its base URL and its key from environment variables. Point both at Mubit, and Claude Code's calls go through Mubit with your Mubit key.

A Claude Pro or Max sign-in can't be used: Mubit refuses sign-in tokens with a `401`. The settings below make Claude Code send your Mubit key instead.

## 1. Set up in the console

Open the Mubit console at [app.mubit.ai](https://app.mubit.ai/) and sign in. If you can't add or create keys, ask an admin of your organization.

1. Open **Provider keys** and add your Anthropic API key, as [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys#add-a-key) shows. Claude Code's calls run on your own Anthropic key. The starter credit doesn't cover Claude Code, because it refuses some of its features, such as web search.
2. Open **Connect**, go to **Mubit key**, and select **Create key**. Copy the key: it starts with `mbt_`, and it's shown only once.

## 2. Set up your computer

On macOS or Linux, add these lines to `~/.zshrc`, or to `~/.bashrc` if you use bash. Then open a new terminal.

```bash
export MUBIT_API_KEY='YOUR_MUBIT_KEY'
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$MUBIT_API_KEY"
export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=claude-haiku-4-5
```

- `MUBIT_API_KEY` holds your Mubit key.
- `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is Mubit's Anthropic base URL. Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows. Leave `/v1` off the end: Claude Code adds it.
- `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` holds your Mubit key. Claude Code sends it in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` turns off Claude Code's telemetry, error reports and automatic updates.
- `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=claude-haiku-4-5` makes Claude Code's small background tasks use Haiku 4.5. Without it, with `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` set, they use your main model.

Use `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, Claude Code sends the key in a background check to `api.anthropic.com`.

> **Warning:** If `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` holds anything but your Mubit key, Claude Code sends it beside your key, and Mubit refuses the call with a `401`. Run `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and don't set it in `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`. If your Claude Code settings file sets it under `env`, remove it there too.

### Keep the key in the Keychain (macOS)

To keep the key out of `~/.zshrc`, store it in the Keychain and read it from there.

Store the key. With `-w` last, the command asks for the key, so the key never sits on a command line or in your shell history:

```bash
security add-generic-password -a "$USER" -s mubit-api-key -w
```

Then, in `~/.zshrc`, replace the `MUBIT_API_KEY` line with this one:

```bash
export MUBIT_API_KEY=$(security find-generic-password -s mubit-api-key -w)
```

## 3. Check it works

In a new terminal, run:

```bash
claude -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
```

It prints `pong`. The call then shows in the console under your project's **Requests**. After that, run `claude` as usual.

## Choose a model

Start Claude Code with `claude --model claude-opus-5-5`, or choose a model with `/model` inside it. Mubit passes the model ID on unchanged.

Tested with Claude Code 2.1.306.

## If a call fails

The error names its code. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting) lists the codes and what to do.


---

<!-- /guides/coding-tools -->

# Coding tools

> Point Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Aider at Mubit with Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/coding-tools.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Each tool on this page reads its base URL and its key from its settings or from environment variables. Point both at Mubit, and the tool's calls go through Mubit with your Mubit key.

Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.

The examples read the key from `MUBIT_API_KEY`. To create a key and set it, follow [step 1 of the Quickstart](/quickstart#1-set-up-in-the-console).

> **Warning:** Send your Mubit key. Subscription sign-ins (Claude Pro or Max, ChatGPT) can't be used: Mubit refuses sign-in tokens with a `401`, and never stores them. The settings below make each tool send your Mubit key instead of a sign-in.

## Claude Code

Claude Code reads Mubit's base URL and your Mubit key from environment variables. [Use Claude Code with Mubit](/guides/claude-code) shows the whole set-up: your Anthropic key under **Provider keys**, a Mubit key, the variables to set, and a first call to check it works.

## Codex

> **Warning:** A ChatGPT sign-in can't be used: Mubit refuses sign-in tokens, including ChatGPT and Codex logins. The provider below makes Codex send the key in `MUBIT_API_KEY` instead.

Add a provider for Mubit to `~/.codex/config.toml`, and make it the default. Put the first two lines at the top of the file, before any `[section]`:

```toml
model = "gpt-6-luna"
model_provider = "mubit"

[model_providers.mubit]
name = "Mubit"
base_url = "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1"
env_key = "MUBIT_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = false
```

- `base_url` is the OpenAI base URL, which ends in `/v1`.
- `env_key` names the environment variable that holds your Mubit key.
- `wire_api = "responses"`: Codex calls the Responses API, which Mubit takes on the same base URL.
- `requires_openai_auth = false`: Codex doesn't ask for an OpenAI sign-in for this provider.

Then start Codex with `codex` in a shell where `MUBIT_API_KEY` is set.

Codex also connects to OpenAI and GitHub directly, for example for its own metrics and update checks. Those connections don't go through Mubit.

Tested with Codex 0.163.0.

## Gemini CLI

> **Note:** If the console doesn't list Gemini under the starter credit, add your Gemini key under **Provider keys** first, as the [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys) page shows. On the starter credit, token counting gets `403 starter_credit_route` and Google Search gets `400 starter_credit_tools`.

> **Warning:** A Google sign-in can't be used: Mubit refuses Google OAuth tokens. Choose the Gemini API key sign-in, as below.

In `~/.gemini/settings.json`, choose the Gemini API key sign-in. It's the **Use Gemini API Key** choice of Gemini CLI's sign-in menu:

```json
{
  "security": {
    "auth": {
      "selectedType": "gemini-api-key"
    }
  }
}
```

Then set these in the shell where you start Gemini CLI, and start it:

```bash
export GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=https://api.mubit.ai/gemini
export GEMINI_API_KEY="$MUBIT_API_KEY"
gemini
```

`GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` is the Gemini base URL. Leave the version path off the end.

Gemini CLI also makes short calls of its own around your prompt, for example to pick a model for it. They show in **Requests** too.

Gemini CLI also sends usage statistics to Google directly. To turn them off, add `"privacy": { "usageStatisticsEnabled": false }` to `~/.gemini/settings.json`.

Tested with Gemini CLI 0.65.0.

## Aider

Aider calls Mubit as an OpenAI-compatible API. Set these in the shell where you start Aider, then start it with your model ID after `openai/`:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_BASE=https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1
export OPENAI_API_KEY="$MUBIT_API_KEY"
aider --model openai/gpt-6-luna
```

The `openai/` prefix tells Aider to call the API at `OPENAI_API_BASE`. Mubit gets the model ID without the prefix.

To use an OpenAI-compatible service such as OpenRouter, set `OPENAI_API_BASE` to the service's base URL from [OpenAI-compatible services](/guides/openai-compatible#base-url), and put the service's model ID after `openai/`.

If Aider warns that it doesn't know the model's context window or costs, it still sends the call.

Aider loads `.env` files from your home folder, repo root and current folder, and their values win over the shell's. Check that none sets `OPENAI_API_BASE` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

Tested with Aider 0.86.2.

## Check the set-up

Start the tool and send one prompt. Then open **Requests** in the console: the call is at the top, and **Model asked** shows the model ID the tool sent.

## If a call fails

The error names its code. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting) lists the codes and what to do.

## Next

- [Frameworks](/guides/frameworks)
- [Keep your model IDs](/guides/model-ids)
- [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys)

<!-- /guides/requests -->

# Find calls in Requests

> Find a call in the console's Requests page, filter the list, read a call's details and its session, and see why a call isn't listed.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/requests.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

**Requests** lists your project's calls, newest first. Open it from the console's sidebar.

Mubit passes each call on and returns the reply. It records the request and reply by default, and Requests shows what served each call.

### The diagram in words

Your app sends a request to Mubit. Mubit passes it on to your model provider, and the reply returns through Mubit to your app. Mubit records the request and reply by default and shows recorded calls in Requests, where **Served by** shows what served each call.

## Filter the list

The row above the list holds the filters:

- the range: `Last 24 hours`, `Last 7 days` or `Last 30 days`;
- **Task**: `All tasks`, or one of your tasks by name;
- **Served by**: who answered each call; `Anyone` lists them all;
- **Errors only**: the calls that got a status of 400 or above;
- **Session**: type a session ID and press Enter to list that session's calls;
- **Clear**: turns off every filter but the range.

The filters live in the page's address, so a reload or a shared link keeps them.

**Errors only** reads the calls already loaded, and the line under the filters says how many of them failed. Select **Load more** to read further.

The chart above the list counts the range's `Calls`, `Errors` or `Response time`. It follows the range and the task only; the other filters narrow the list.

## The list

Each row is one call, with its `Time`, `Task`, `Model asked`, `Served by`, `Response` time, `Status` and `Rating`. A call that no task holds yet shows `—` under `Task`.

**Load more**, under the list, reads older calls.

## Read a call's details

Select a row. The call opens in a panel on the right. Its head is the task's name, or `Request` while no task holds it, with the call's time and the model asked. The panel shows:

- **Status**: the HTTP status and what it was, such as `200 · answered` or `400 · provider error`;
- **Response**: the call's time from start to end;
- **Tokens**: the tokens in and out;
- **Request**: the last user message of the call;
- **Reply**: the answer's text;
- **Where the time went**: how the call's time divides between Mubit and the model that answered;
- **Rate this reply**: `Good` or `Bad`;
- **Details**: the call's **Request** and **Session** IDs, each with a copy button.

**Open as a page** opens the call on a page of its own. **Close** or Escape closes the panel.

## A call's session

**Details** shows the call's **Session**. **Requests in this session**, on the call's page, lists the calls that share it. You can also type the session ID in the **Session** filter.

[Tasks and sessions](/guides/tasks-and-sessions#group-a-conversations-calls-into-a-session) shows how Mubit gives each call a session, and how to name one yourself.

## Find a call's request ID

Every answer from Mubit carries the call's request ID in the `x-middleware-request-id` header: a success, a stream, your provider's error, and Mubit's own error. Mubit's own errors also carry it in their body. It starts with `mreq_`. Quote it when you ask for help with a call.

To read it:

```python [Python]
raw = client.chat.completions.with_raw_response.create(
    model="gpt-6-luna",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the word ok."}],
)
print("request id:", raw.headers.get("x-middleware-request-id"))
response = raw.parse()
```

```ts [TypeScript]
const { data, response } = await client.chat.completions
  .create({
    model: "gpt-6-luna",
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Reply with the word ok." }],
  })
  .withResponse();
console.log("request id:", response.headers.get("x-middleware-request-id"));
```

```bash [curl]
curl -i https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "gpt-6-luna", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the word ok."}]}'
```

The Python and TypeScript examples use the client from [Connect OpenAI](/guides/connect-openai). In curl, `-i` prints the answer's headers. The header works the same way on Anthropic, Gemini and the OpenAI-compatible services.

> **Note:** The **Request** ID under **Details** is the console's own ID for the call. It is not the request ID your app gets in `x-middleware-request-id`.

## Why a call isn't listed

- **You just sent it.** Reload **Requests**.
- **It's older than the range.** Choose a longer range.
- **Mubit refused it before calling your provider.** A call refused for its key, its path or a missing provider key leaves no record. Look up its code in [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting).
- **It sent `x-middleware-store: false`, or `x-middleware-record` set to `metadata` or `off`.** Mubit keeps no request or answer for such a call, and never lists it.
- **It asked for a list of models.** Model lists don't show on **Requests**.


---

<!-- /guides/tasks-and-sessions -->

# Tasks and sessions

> How Mubit groups your calls into tasks, and how to group a conversation's calls into one session.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/tasks-and-sessions.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Mubit finds tasks in your calls by itself. This page shows what decides a call's task, and how to tell Mubit which calls belong to one conversation.

## What makes a task

Calls form one task when they share all of these:

- their instructions;
- their tools;
- their tool choice;
- their output format;
- their model.

The rest of the call doesn't count: the messages after the instructions, and settings such as `temperature` or `max_tokens`. For the model, see [Keep your model IDs](/guides/model-ids).

The instructions are the system prompt: `system` on Anthropic; the `system` and `developer` messages on OpenAI Chat Completions; `instructions` and the `system` and `developer` input items on OpenAI Responses; `systemInstruction` on Gemini.

**Tasks** shows each task under a short name made from the first words of its instructions.

Mubit reads the instructions with a few allowances, so one kind of call keeps one task:

- Runs of spaces and line breaks count as one space.
- Numbers, dates, times and IDs don't split a task.
- Other words that change from call to call do: a customer's name in the instructions makes one task per name.

> **Tip:** Put the text that changes per call, such as a name, in the user message, not in the instructions.

## Group a conversation's calls into a session

A session is the calls of one conversation. Mubit sets a task's test cases aside by session.

Mubit gives each call a session. It takes the first of these that the call has:

1. `metadata.thread_id`
2. `metadata.session_id`
3. `metadata.conversation_id`
4. On Anthropic, `metadata.user_id`
5. On OpenAI Responses, `prompt_cache_key`

A call with none of these gets a session from the start of its conversation: its instructions and its first user message. When each call sends the conversation so far, its later turns repeat them, so its calls share a session without any field. If your app sends only the new message, for example with Responses' `previous_response_id`, send `metadata.session_id`.

Which field to send:

| Provider | Field |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `metadata.session_id`, or `metadata.thread_id` or `metadata.conversation_id` |
| Anthropic | `metadata.user_id`, the one `metadata` field Anthropic takes |
| Gemini | None: Mubit uses the start of the conversation |

On Anthropic, if your app already sends `metadata.user_id` as an ID for your end user, all of that user's conversations become one session.

Mubit trims each value. A value longer than 200 characters is kept as a hash.

## Example

This call names its session `ticket-1042`:

```python [Python]
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MUBIT_API_KEY"],
)

instructions = (
    "Sort the support message into one category: "
    "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-6-luna",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": instructions},
        {"role": "user", "content": "I cannot sign in since I changed my email address."},
    ],
    metadata={"session_id": "ticket-1042"},
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

```ts [TypeScript]
import OpenAI from "openai";

const apiKey = process.env.MUBIT_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error("MUBIT_API_KEY is not set");

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1",
  apiKey,
});

const instructions =
  "Sort the support message into one category: " +
  "billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only.";

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
  messages: [
    { role: "system", content: instructions },
    { role: "user", content: "I cannot sign in since I changed my email address." },
  ],
  metadata: { session_id: "ticket-1042" },
});
console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
```

```bash [curl]
curl https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUBIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "metadata": {"session_id": "ticket-1042"},
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Sort the support message into one category: billing, bug, account or other. Reply with the category only."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "I cannot sign in since I changed my email address."}
    ]
  }'
```

The TypeScript example uses top-level `await`, so run it as an ES module: save the file as `tasks.mts` and run `npx tsx tasks.mts`, or add `"type": "module"` to your `package.json`.

## See a call's session

1. In the console, open **Requests**.
2. Select the call's row.
3. Open **Details**. **Session** shows the call's session.

To list one session's calls, enter its ID in the **Session** filter on **Requests**. See [Find calls in Requests](/guides/requests#a-calls-session).

## If a call fails

The error names its code. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting) lists the codes and what to do.

<!-- /guides/model-ids -->

# Keep your model IDs

> Your app keeps the model IDs it sends today. What Mubit does with them, how they shape tasks, and what the starter credit serves.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/model-ids.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

You don't change the model IDs in your code. Send the IDs you send today, such as `gpt-6-luna`, `claude-haiku-4-5` or `gemini-3.8-flash`.

## What Mubit does with a model ID

- **It passes the ID on.** When Mubit sends a call to your provider, it sends your model ID as your app wrote it.
- **It records the ID.** In **Requests**, **Model asked** shows the model ID of each call.
- **It counts the model in the task.** Calls form one task when they share their instructions, tools, tool choice, output format and model. So the same instructions sent to two different models make two tasks.

Mubit reads the model without its date or snapshot suffix, and without `-latest`. For example, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` and `claude-haiku-4-5` count as one model, and so do `gpt-5.5-2026-04-23` and `gpt-5.5`.

On Gemini, the model ID is in the path, as in `/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:generateContent`. Mubit reads it from there.

## On the starter credit

The starter credit serves a set list of models for each provider it covers. A call that names another model gets `400 starter_credit_model`, and the message lists the models it serves. A dated ID works only when that list names it.

With your own provider key, you can use any model your provider account can use. See [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys).

## What you can't do with a model ID

There is no Mubit model ID: you can't send a call to an adapter by naming it as the model. To try an adapter, compare it in **Try models**: see [Compare with your provider](/guides/first-adapter#4-compare-with-your-provider).


---

<!-- /guides/import-past-calls -->

# Import past calls

> Import past model calls from Langfuse, Braintrust or Pydantic Logfire with a read-only key, so Mubit can find tasks in them.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/guides/import-past-calls.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

If your app's calls are already in an observability tool, you can import them. Mubit treats imported calls like the calls your app sends: it finds tasks in them. The import reads from Langfuse, Braintrust or Pydantic Logfire with a read-only key.

Only an admin of your organization can import calls. A member sees `An admin of your organization imports calls.`

## Before you start

Create a read-only key in your tool:

| Tool | Key to create |
| --- | --- |
| Langfuse | A project API key with the Viewer permission |
| Braintrust | A service token in the Viewers group |
| Pydantic Logfire | A read token |

For Langfuse, paste the key in the form the field's placeholder shows: `pk-lf-...:sk-lf-...`.

## Start an import

1. In the console's sidebar, open **Import past calls**.
2. Under **Source**, choose your tool: **Langfuse**, **Braintrust** or **Pydantic Logfire**.
3. Choose the host your tool's account is on, such as your Langfuse host.
4. Paste your read-only key in **Read-only key**.
5. To test the key first, select **Check key**. A working key shows `Accepted`, with the newest call and the models it found.
6. Under **Window**, choose how far back to read: **7 days**, **14 days** or **30 days**.
7. Select the box that starts `I may share these calls with Mubit.`
8. To keep the key for the next import, select **Keep the key for later imports**.
9. Select **Start import**.

## What the import reads

- The calls in the window you chose.
- Only the calls from before your project's first call through Mubit. The page says `Cut at the project's first live call.`
- Mubit sends your tool read requests only. A request outside the tool's read-only list is stopped, and the import fails.

Your project runs one import at a time. To start another, wait for the first to end, or cancel it.

## Follow the import

The page shows the newest import with its state: `Queued`, `Running`, `Paused`, `Done`, `Failed` or `Cancelled`. While it runs, a line counts the calls read, imported and skipped, and the tasks found. The page updates by itself.

- To stop an import, select **Cancel**.
- A `Paused` import says why it paused. When your tool limits the rate, the page says when the import resumes.
- A `Failed` import says why it failed.

When the import is done, the page shows how many calls it imported into how many tasks. Open **Tasks** to see them.

## The key

After you save the key, the page shows only `••••` and its last 4 characters.

When an import ends, Mubit deletes the key, unless you chose **Keep the key for later imports**. The last line says which: `The key was deleted.` or `The key was kept.`


---

<!-- /admin/projects -->

# Projects

> Your workspace's one project, what it holds, and how an admin renames it.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/admin/projects.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

## Your project

Your workspace belongs to your organization, and it has one project. Mubit makes the project when your workspace is set up. The project holds your app's calls, keys and tasks.

You can't add a second project or delete this one. The console offers neither.

Your Mubit keys work for this project only.

## Rename the project

An admin can rename the project:

1. In the sidebar, under **Workspace**, open **Projects**.
2. On the project's row, open the menu.
3. Select **Rename…**.
4. Enter the new name in **Project name**: 1 to 100 characters.
5. Select **Save**.

**Get started** has a **Rename** button too, in its head.

[Members and roles](/admin/members) lists what else only admins can do.


---

<!-- /admin/members -->

# Members and roles

> The two roles in your organization, what only admins can do, what a member sees instead, that the console can't add, change or remove people, and when the console signs you out.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/admin/members.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Each person in your organization is an `Admin` or a `Member`. The account menu, at the foot of the sidebar, shows your role.

## What only admins can do

- create, rotate and revoke Mubit keys, under **Mubit keys**;
- add, rotate and delete provider keys, under **Provider keys**;
- import past calls, under **Import past calls**;
- change **Settings**, in the project's sidebar under **Set up**. **Settings** shows there once training is on for your workspace;
- rename the project.

## What members can do

Members can do the rest. For example, they can read **Requests**, **Tasks**, **Adapters** and **Settings**, use **Try models**, and open **Connect**.

Where a page has an admin's action, a member sees a line in its place, such as `Ask an admin of {org} for a key. Admins create, rotate and revoke keys.` on **Mubit keys**, with your organization's name.

When a member tries an admin's action, the console says `Only an admin of {org} can do this.` On **Settings**, a member reads `Only admins of {org} can change settings.`

## Add people, change a role or remove someone

The console has no controls to invite a person, change someone's role or remove a member. Not even an admin can make these changes in the console.

To make one of these changes, ask for help, as [Get help](/troubleshooting#get-help) shows.

## Sign-out after inactivity

After 15 minutes without a key press, a click, a touch or a scroll in any of the console's tabs, the console signs you out. The sign-in screen then reads `Signed out after 15 minutes without activity.` Sign in again to go on.

The console remembers your last activity across page loads: opened again more than 15 minutes later, it signs you out at once.


---

<!-- /admin/mubit-keys -->

# Mubit keys

> Create, rotate and revoke the Mubit keys your apps send, choose between inference and read-only keys, replace a key without stopping your app, and read the key list.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/admin/mubit-keys.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Your app sends a Mubit key in place of a provider key. Each key works for your project only.

Only an admin creates, rotates and revokes keys. A member sees `Ask an admin of {org} for a key. Admins create, rotate and revoke keys.` in place of the buttons.

## Create a key

1. In the sidebar, open **Mubit keys**.
2. Select **Create key**.
3. Enter a **Name**, such as the name of your app.
4. Leave **Permission** at **Inference: calls this project**.
5. Select **Create key**.
6. Copy the key. The console says `Copy this key now. It won't be shown again.`

## Inference and read-only keys

A key has one of two permissions. You choose it when you create the key.

- **Inference: calls this project**: for apps that send calls. Your app needs this one.
- **Read only: reads its records**: reads this project's records. Calls sent with it are refused with `403 key_permission`.

## The key list

Each row shows a key's:

- **Name**;
- **Key**: its first characters and a mask, never the whole key;
- **Permission**: `Inference` or `Read only`;
- **Created**;
- **Expires**: the date the key stops working, or `never`;
- **Last used**: `never`, or up to about 90 seconds behind the key's last call;
- **Status**: `Active`, `Revoked` or `Expired`.

Before a key's **Expires** date, replace it, as [Replace a key without stopping your app](#replace-a-key-without-stopping-your-app) shows.

## Rotate a key

Rotating gives a key a new secret. The key keeps its name and its permission, and its lifetime starts again from now.

Rotating leaves no time to switch over. Mubit stops accepting the old secret within about 30 seconds, and the dialog says how soon. An app that still sends the old secret then gets `401 invalid_key`. To change the key of an app that is running, follow [Replace a key without stopping your app](#replace-a-key-without-stopping-your-app) instead.

1. On the key's row, open the menu.
2. Select **Rotate…**. The dialog `Rotate {name}?` opens and says how soon the old secret stops working.
3. Select **Rotate key**.
4. Copy the new secret. It is shown once.
5. Put the new secret in your app.

You can rotate an active or an expired key. A revoked key can't be rotated: create a new key instead.

## Replace a key without stopping your app

Rotating stops the old secret within seconds. For an app that is running, use a second key:

1. [Create a key](#create-a-key) with the same permission.
2. Put the new key in your app, and deploy it.
3. Check that the app's calls work with the new key. Its **Last used** shows a time within about 90 seconds of its first call.
4. [Revoke](#revoke-a-key) the old key.

## Revoke a key

1. On the key's row, open the menu.
2. Select **Revoke…**. The dialog `Revoke {name}?` opens.
3. Select **Revoke key**.

The key's status reads `Revoked`. The line under the list says how soon Mubit refuses a revoked key: `A revoked key is refused within a minute.` After that, calls with the key get `401 invalid_key`.

> **Note:** The console can't turn a revoked key back on or rotate it. To call again, create a new key and put it in your app.


---

<!-- /admin/provider-keys -->

# Provider keys

> Add your own Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or OpenAI-compatible service key in the console, so Mubit calls the provider on your own account.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/admin/provider-keys.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Your app sends Mubit your Mubit key. Mubit then calls the provider with your provider key, so the calls are on your own provider account.

You add provider keys in the console, under **Provider keys**. Your app's code doesn't change.

## Which providers need a key

The starter credit covers some providers, and the console names them: **Get started**, for example, reads `Calls to {providers} use the starter credit until you add a key.`

| Provider | Without your own key |
| --- | --- |
| A provider the starter credit covers | Calls use the starter credit while it lasts. |
| A provider it doesn't cover | Calls get `403 provider_key_missing`. |

Once you add your own key for a provider, its calls use your key.

Some options, such as hosted web search, file search and stored prompts, are not available on the starter credit. The error says which, and your own key removes the limit. See [Starter credit errors](/troubleshooting#starter-credit-errors).

## Add a key

Only an admin of your organization can add, rotate or delete provider keys. A member sees `Ask an admin of {org} to add or change keys.`, with your organization's name.

1. In the sidebar, under **Workspace**, open **Provider keys**.
2. Select **Add key**. The dialog **Add a provider key** opens.
3. Choose the **Provider**: **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **Gemini** or **OpenAI-compatible**.
4. For **OpenAI-compatible**, choose the **Service**: **OpenRouter**, **Groq**, **Together** or **Mistral**.
5. Paste the key in **API key**.
6. To name the key, enter a **Label (optional)**.
7. Select **Check and save**.

Mubit checks the key with the provider before it saves anything. A good key shows `Valid`. A refused key shows `Refused`, and nothing is saved.

Each provider takes one key. A provider that has one is off in the **Provider** menu, with `It has a key already.` To change the key, rotate it.

### The key must be an API key

Paste an API key, not a sign-in token. Subscription sign-ins, such as Claude Pro or Max and ChatGPT, can't be used: the dialog answers `Not an API key`. A Mubit key there gets `Mubit key`, and another provider's key gets `Wrong provider`.

## What the page shows

Mubit stores each key encrypted. After saving, only its last 4 characters show.

Each key's row shows details such as its provider, its last 4 characters and its fingerprint: `fp` and a short hash of the key. Each call's record keeps the fingerprint of the key it used.

While the starter credit covers a provider you have no key for, a box at the top reads **Starter credit** with `Available`. Once the credit is used up, it reads `Used up`: add your own key to keep calling that provider.

## Rotate a key

1. On the key's row, select **Rotate**.
2. Paste the new key in **New API key**.
3. Select **Check and replace**.

Mubit checks the new key, then calls the provider with it. Revoke the old key at the provider afterwards.

## Delete a key

1. On the key's row, open the menu next to **Rotate**.
2. Select **Delete…**.
3. Type the key's name, as the dialog asks.
4. Select **Delete key**.

Mubit stops calling the provider with that key. Deleting it here doesn't revoke it at the provider: revoke it there too.


---

<!-- /reference/api -->

# API reference

> The Mubit API in one place. Base URL, keys, paths per provider, the headers Mubit reads and sends, model IDs, streaming, limits, retries, sizes and the error format.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/reference/api.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Mubit takes each provider's own API. Your app sends the requests it sends today to Mubit's base URL, under the provider's prefix, with a Mubit key in place of the provider key. Mubit records each call.

## Base URL

```
https://api.mubit.ai
```

Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows.

Call Mubit from your server, not from a browser. The API answers no CORS preflight request, so a browser refuses to send the call.

## Keys

Send your Mubit key in the header your provider's SDK uses for its own key. A Mubit key starts with `mbt_`.

| Provider | Header |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible services | `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MUBIT_KEY` |
| Anthropic | `x-api-key: YOUR_MUBIT_KEY`, or `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MUBIT_KEY` |
| Gemini | `x-goog-api-key: YOUR_MUBIT_KEY` |

Send one key, and only your Mubit key. Mubit refuses a call with a `401` when it carries:

- no key (`missing_key`);
- a key that is wrong, revoked or malformed, or two different Mubit keys (`invalid_key`);
- a provider's API key, a sign-in token, or another credential beside your Mubit key (see [Key errors](/troubleshooting#key-errors));
- your Mubit key somewhere else in the request, such as another header or the path (`middleware_key_refused`).

For Gemini, send the key in the header, not in `?key=`.

Your provider keys stay in the console. Add them under **Provider keys**, as the [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys) page shows.

## Paths

Each provider has a prefix. After it, use the provider's own path.

| Provider | Prefix | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `/openai/v1` | `POST /openai/v1/chat/completions`, `POST /openai/v1/responses`, `POST /openai/v1/embeddings`, `GET /openai/v1/models` |
| Anthropic | `/anthropic` | `POST /anthropic/v1/messages`, `POST /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens`, `GET /anthropic/v1/models` |
| Gemini | `/gemini` | `POST /gemini/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`, `POST /gemini/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`, `GET /gemini/v1beta/models` |
| OpenAI-compatible services | `/compat/{service}/v1` | `POST /compat/openrouter/v1/chat/completions` |

So the base URL for an SDK is:

| SDK | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `https://api.mubit.ai/openai/v1` |
| Anthropic | `https://api.mubit.ai/anthropic` |
| Gemini (google-genai) | `https://api.mubit.ai/gemini` |
| OpenAI SDK on Gemini | `https://api.mubit.ai/gemini/v1beta/openai` |
| OpenAI SDK on an OpenAI-compatible service | `https://api.mubit.ai/compat/{service}/v1` |

### OpenAI-compatible services

`{service}` is `openrouter`, `groq`, `together` or `mistral`. Under `/compat/{service}/v1`, Mubit serves `POST /chat/completions`, `POST /embeddings`, `GET /models` and `GET /models/{id}`. These services need your own key, unless the console lists the service under the starter credit. See [OpenAI-compatible services](/guides/openai-compatible).

### Paths Mubit refuses

| Answer | When |
| --- | --- |
| `404 unknown_route` | The path is outside the prefixes above, or a `/compat` path or method that isn't listed. |
| `404 unknown_provider` | The `{service}` in a `/compat` path isn't one of the four. The message lists them. |
| `403 admin_path_refused` | An organization or admin endpoint of the provider. Call the provider directly for those. |
| `400 invalid_path` | The path has a `.` or `..` segment, a `;`, a control character, or an escape that decodes again. |

On the starter credit, fewer paths work. After the prefix: on Anthropic, `POST /v1/messages`, `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` and `GET /v1/models`; on OpenAI, `POST /chat/completions`, `POST /responses`, `POST /embeddings` and `GET /models`; on Gemini, `POST /{version}/models/{model}:generateContent` and `:streamGenerateContent`, where `{version}` is a version such as `v1beta` or `v1`; on an OpenAI-compatible service, `POST /chat/completions` and `GET /models`. Any other path gets `403 starter_credit_route` until you add your own key for that provider. A provider the starter credit doesn't cover always needs your own key; the console names the providers it covers. See the [starter credit's errors](/troubleshooting#starter-credit-errors).

## Request headers Mubit reads

Mubit reads these optional headers, and doesn't send them to your provider:

| Header | Values | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x-middleware-store` | `false`, `0`, `off` or `no` | Mubit keeps a record of the call without its request and answer. |
| `x-middleware-record` | `full`, `metadata` or `off` | How much of the call Mubit keeps. `metadata` is the same as `x-middleware-store: false`; `off` also drops the call's task fingerprint. |

A header can lower what Mubit keeps of a call, never raise it. When a call sends several values, the lowest one counts.

Mubit passes most other headers to the provider as you sent them, such as `anthropic-version` and `anthropic-beta`. In particular:

- it never sends a header that starts with `x-middleware-` to your provider;
- it takes out your Mubit key, and sends your provider key or the starter credit's key in its place;
- it doesn't pass on cookies, in either direction;
- it doesn't pass on forwarding headers, such as `forwarded`, `x-forwarded-for`, `x-real-ip` and `via`.

## Response headers

| Header | On | What it says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x-middleware-request-id` | Every answer: a success, a stream, your provider's error, Mubit's own error | The call's ID in Mubit: `mreq_` and 32 hex digits. IDs sort by time. |
| `x-should-retry` | Mubit's errors that a retry won't fix, such as the key errors | `false`. |
| `retry-after` | Mubit's `429` and `503` errors | Seconds to wait before you try again. |

Your provider's own headers, such as its `request-id` or `x-request-id`, pass unchanged beside them.

Quote the `x-middleware-request-id` when you ask for help with a call. [Find a call's request ID](/guides/requests#find-a-calls-request-id) shows how to read it in Python, TypeScript and curl.

## Model IDs

Send the model IDs you send today. When Mubit sends a call to your provider, it sends your model ID as your app wrote it, and records it. On Gemini, the model ID is in the path.

There is no Mubit model ID. On the starter credit, a call must name a model the starter credit serves: another model gets `400 starter_credit_model`, and the message lists the models. See [Keep your model IDs](/guides/model-ids).

## Streaming

Stream as you do with your provider: set `stream` to true on OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible services and Anthropic, or call `streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` on Gemini. Mubit passes the stream to your app as it arrives.

Each provider page shows an example: [OpenAI](/guides/connect-openai#stream-the-answer), [Anthropic](/guides/connect-anthropic#stream-the-answer), [Gemini](/guides/connect-gemini#stream-the-answer).

## Limits

Mubit's limits today:

| Limit | Value | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connect to the provider | 10 s | Mubit tries once more on a new connection. If that fails too, the call gets `502 upstream_unreachable`, and nothing was sent. |
| First byte | 610 s | From the start of your request to the provider's status and headers. Past it, the call gets `504 upstream_timeout`. |
| Silence | 15 minutes | The longest time no part of the answer goes to your app, because the provider is quiet or your app stopped reading. Past it, Mubit closes the connection. |
| Total | 60 minutes | The longest a call can run, from the start of the request to the last byte of the answer. Past it, Mubit closes the connection. |

When Mubit closes a stream at a limit, the connection breaks. Mubit adds nothing to the stream.

The OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs wait 600 s by default, so their own timeout usually ends a wait for the first byte before Mubit's does.

## Retries

Mubit retries a call once, and only when the first try failed before any byte of the request was sent: the connection to the provider couldn't be made. It never retries a call once the request has started, because the provider may already have it, and a second send could be billed twice.

Your SDK owns retries. Mubit's errors tell it what to do: `x-should-retry: false` on errors a retry won't fix, and `retry-after` on `429` and `503`.

## Sizes

On the starter credit, Mubit checks each request body before it sends the call. The body must:

- be at most 8 MiB, or the call gets `413 starter_credit_body`;
- arrive whole within 60 s, or the call gets `408 starter_credit_body`;
- be sent as plain JSON, with no content encoding, and be one JSON object, or the call gets `400 starter_credit_body`.

With your own provider key, Mubit doesn't make these checks.

Today, Mubit records up to 32 MiB of a request, and the first 4 MiB and the last 256 KiB of an answer. A bigger call still goes through whole. Only Mubit's record of it is cut.

## Errors

Mubit passes your provider's answers back to your app, its errors included.

Mubit's own errors use your provider's error format, so your SDK reads them as it reads the provider's. Each one has the type `middleware_gateway_error`, a `code`, a message, and the call's request ID. The one exception is a call sent to the console's address: it gets `503 no_provider_configured`, with the type `middleware_error`. [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting#mubits-errors) lists every code and what to do.

The format depends on the path:

| Path | Format |
| --- | --- |
| `/openai/…`, `/compat/…`, `/gemini/v1beta/openai/…`, and every other path, such as one that gets `404 unknown_route` | OpenAI's |
| `/anthropic/…` | Anthropic's |
| `/gemini/…`, except its OpenAI-compatible endpoint | Gemini's |

```json [OpenAI]
{
  "error": {
    "message": "No API key was provided. Send your Mubit key where the provider's SDK sends its API key.",
    "type": "middleware_gateway_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "missing_key",
    "request_id": "mreq_…"
  }
}
```

```json [Anthropic]
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "middleware_gateway_error",
    "message": "No API key was provided. Send your Mubit key where the provider's SDK sends its API key.",
    "code": "missing_key"
  },
  "request_id": "mreq_…"
}
```

```json [Gemini]
{
  "error": {
    "code": 401,
    "message": "No API key was provided. Send your Mubit key where the provider's SDK sends its API key.",
    "status": "UNAUTHENTICATED",
    "details": [
      {
        "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo",
        "reason": "missing_key",
        "domain": "middleware.now",
        "metadata": { "type": "middleware_gateway_error" }
      },
      {
        "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.RequestInfo",
        "requestId": "mreq_…"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

In Gemini's format, the HTTP status is the error's `code`, and Mubit's code is the `reason` of its `ErrorInfo` detail.

> **Note:** An error whose type is `middleware_gateway_error` or `middleware_error` came from Mubit. An error without either, on an answer that carries `x-middleware-request-id`, came from your provider as it sent it. An answer without that header didn't come through Mubit's API: check the base URL and try again.


---

<!-- /troubleshooting -->

# Troubleshooting

> Common problems by what you see, every error code Mubit sends and what to do about it, provider problems that make a call fail, request IDs, and how to ask for help.

<!-- Auto-generated from pages/troubleshooting.mdx — do not edit by hand. -->

Start from what you see. Every error from Mubit names a `code`: find it under [Mubit's errors](#mubits-errors).

## Common problems

### The call gets a 401, such as `missing_key` or `invalid_key`

Mubit refused the call's key. The error's code says why:

- `missing_key`: the call carries no key. If your code reads `MUBIT_API_KEY`, set it in the shell that runs the code.
- `invalid_key`: copy the key again, or create a new one. Check the base URL against your console's **Connect** page.
- A code that ends in `_refused`: the call carries something other than your Mubit key, such as a provider key or a sign-in token, or your Mubit key in the wrong place. With the Anthropic SDKs, check `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`: unset it, or set it to your Mubit key. With Claude Code, unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` instead (see [Coding tools](/guides/coding-tools#claude-code)).
- No `middleware_gateway_error` in the error: your provider refused the provider key saved for this project. An admin checks it under **Provider keys**.

Sign-ins to Claude Pro or Max, ChatGPT or Codex can't be used. Use a Mubit key. See [Key errors](#key-errors).

### The call gets a 403, such as `provider_key_missing`

If the error's type is `middleware_gateway_error`, Mubit refused the call. Its code says why:

- `provider_key_missing`: this project has no key for that provider. A provider the starter credit doesn't cover always needs your own key; the console names the providers it covers. An admin adds it under **Provider keys**, as [Add a key](/admin/provider-keys#add-a-key) shows.
- `key_permission`: the key is read-only. Use an **Inference** key.
- `key_scope`: the key isn't tied to one project. Use a key created in the project the calls are for.
- `starter_credit_route`: the starter credit doesn't serve that path. Add your own key for the provider.
- `admin_path_refused`: the path is an organization or admin endpoint. Call your provider directly for those.

Without `middleware_gateway_error`, your provider refused it: see [Your provider's errors](#your-providers-errors). See also [Provider key errors](#provider-key-errors) and [Key errors](#key-errors).

### My call isn't in Requests

- **The call didn't go through Mubit.** Check that your client uses Mubit's base URL. An answer from Mubit carries the header `x-middleware-request-id`.
- **The call asked Mubit not to keep it.** A call sent with `x-middleware-store: false`, or with `x-middleware-record: metadata` or `off`, doesn't show in **Requests**.
- **Mubit refused it before calling your provider.** A call refused for its key, its path or a missing provider key leaves no record, so it isn't in **Requests**. Read the error your app got. See [Why a call isn't listed](/guides/requests#why-a-call-isnt-listed).

### A call from a browser fails

Mubit's API answers no CORS preflight request, so a browser refuses to send the call. Call Mubit from your server. That also keeps your key off your users' devices.

### A long call or stream stops

Mubit has [time limits](/reference/api#limits): 610 s for the provider to start its answer, 15 minutes with no part of the answer going to your app, and 60 minutes in all.

- `504 upstream_timeout`: the provider didn't start its answer within 610 s. For long answers, stream: a stream starts as soon as the provider starts writing. Your SDK's own timeout (600 s by default for OpenAI and Anthropic) usually ends the wait first: raise it, or stream.
- A stream that breaks off: it went 15 minutes without sending anything, or ran for 60 minutes. Make sure your app keeps reading the stream.

### The call gets a 502, 503 or 504

- `503` with the type `middleware_gateway_error`: wait the seconds in `retry-after`, then try again. Nothing was sent to your provider. A `503` with the type `middleware_error` is [`no_provider_configured`](#path-errors). Any other `503` is your provider's.
- `502 upstream_unreachable`: Mubit couldn't connect to your provider. Nothing was sent. Try again shortly.
- `502 upstream_failed`: the connection broke after the request started. Your provider may have the request, so Mubit doesn't send it again. Try again if a second call is safe for your app.
- `504 upstream_timeout`: see [A long call or stream stops](#a-long-call-or-stream-stops).

### Calls on the starter credit are refused

The starter credit serves a set list of models, paths and options. Each refusal names what it doesn't serve: change the call as the message says, or add your own key for the provider under **Provider keys**. See [Starter credit errors](#starter-credit-errors).

### My SDK retries a call Mubit refused

Mubit sends `x-should-retry: false` on errors a retry won't fix, and `retry-after` on `429` and `503`. SDKs that read these headers stop or wait. Your SDK owns retries: Mubit itself retries only a call it couldn't send at all. See [Retries](/reference/api#retries).

### A task doesn't train, or an adapter isn't in Try models

Open the task in **Tasks**, or the adapter in **Adapters**, and read its status. [Create your first adapter](/guides/first-adapter) explains each one and what to do:

- [What each test result means](/guides/first-adapter#test-results): `Passed`, `Below target`, `Malformed tool calls`, `Prompt only` and `Not tested`.
- [Why a task is waiting or cannot train](/guides/first-adapter#waits-and-recovery): the daily training limit, the pause between trainings, and too few or too long examples.
- [Why an adapter is unavailable in Try models](/guides/first-adapter#try-models-unavailable): the console's messages, such as `Not in Try models: prompt only`, and what each one means.

## Mubit's errors

Mubit's own errors use your provider's error format. Their `type` is `middleware_gateway_error`, and they name a `code` and the call's request ID. The one exception is `no_provider_configured`, under [Path errors](#path-errors): its type is `middleware_error`. The [API reference](/reference/api#errors) shows the format for each provider.

In the messages, `{provider}` is the provider's name, such as `OpenAI` or `Anthropic`. `{upstream}` is the provider's name, or `this workspace's gateway`. An ellipsis (…) marks text left out here.

### Key errors

| Code | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `missing_key` | 401 | No API key was provided. Send your Mubit key where the provider's SDK sends its API key. | Pass your Mubit key to the client, or set `MUBIT_API_KEY` in the shell that runs your code. |
| `invalid_key` | 401 | Incorrect API key provided. | The key is wrong, revoked or malformed, or the call carries two different Mubit keys. Copy the key again, or create a new one under **Mubit keys**. Check the base URL against your console's **Connect** page. |
| `wrong_region` | 401 | Names the base URL to send the call to. | Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows. |
| `key_expired` | 401 | This API key expired at `{time}`. Create a new key or rotate this one. | Create a new key, or ask an admin to rotate this one under **Mubit keys**. |
| `key_permission` | 403 | This key's permission can't call a provider. Use an inference key of this project. | The key is read-only. An admin creates an **Inference** key under **Mubit keys**. |
| `key_scope` | 403 | This key is not tied to one project. Use an inference key created for one project. | Use a key created in the project the calls are for. |
| `provider_key_refused` | 401 | This is a provider API key, not a Mubit key. Send your Mubit key where your SDK sends its API key, and add the provider key under Provider keys in the console. | Send your Mubit key. Add the provider key under **Provider keys**. |
| `subscription_token_refused` | 401 | This is a Claude subscription sign-in token (from a Claude login or claude setup-token), not a Mubit key. … | Claude Pro and Max sign-ins can't be used. Send your Mubit key. |
| `jwt_refused` | 401 | This is a sign-in token (a JWT), not a Mubit key. … | Sign-ins such as ChatGPT and Codex logins can't be used. Send your Mubit key. |
| `oauth_token_refused` | 401 | This is a Google OAuth token, not a Mubit key. Send your Mubit key where your SDK sends its API key. | Send your Mubit key in place of the Google sign-in. |
| `extra_credential_refused` | 401 | This request carries a credential that is not a Mubit key beside your Mubit key. Send only the Mubit key. | Remove the other credential. With the Anthropic SDKs, unset `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or set it to your Mubit key. With Claude Code, unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` instead (see [Coding tools](/guides/coding-tools#claude-code)). |
| `middleware_key_refused` | 401 | This request carries a Mubit key outside the places the gateway reads keys from. Send your Mubit key where your SDK sends its API key, and only there. | Send the key only in the [key header](/reference/api#keys) for your provider. |
| `engine_unavailable` | 503 | The gateway could not check this key just now. Try again shortly. | Wait the seconds in `retry-after`, then try again. |

### Provider key errors

| Code | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider_key_missing` | 403 | This project has no `{provider}` key. Add one under Provider keys in the console. | Add the provider's key under **Provider keys**, as the [Provider keys](/admin/provider-keys#add-a-key) page shows. |
| `provider_region_unavailable` | 403 | … Delete the key and add it again under Provider keys in the console. | Delete the provider's key under **Provider keys**, then add it again. |
| `key_store_unavailable` | 503 | The gateway could not read this project's provider key just now. Try again shortly. | Wait the seconds in `retry-after`, then try again. |

### Starter credit errors

These come only on calls the starter credit pays for.

| Code | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `starter_credit_used_up` | 402 | The starter credit on … `{provider}` key is used up. Add your own `{provider}` key under Provider keys in the console … | Add your own key for that provider under **Provider keys**. Your calls use it from then on. |
| `starter_credit_model` | 400 | The starter credit serves these `{provider}` models on this route: … Name one of them as the model, or add your own `{provider}` key under Provider keys in the console to use another. | Use a model the message lists, or add your own key. |
| `starter_credit_route` | 403 | This route is not available on the starter credit. Add your own `{provider}` key under Provider keys in the console to use it. | The starter credit serves fewer paths; [Paths Mubit refuses](/reference/api#paths-mubit-refuses) lists them. Add your own key for other paths. |
| `starter_credit_tools` | 400 | Tools billed apart from tokens (hosted web search, file search, code execution, image generation, hosted MCP), tool versions the starter credit does not list, and background mode are not available on the starter credit. … | Leave those tools and background mode out, or add your own key. |
| `starter_credit_option` | 400 | Names one option the starter credit doesn't serve, and how to leave it out. | Change the call as the message says, or add your own key. |
| `starter_credit_body` | 413, 408 or 400 | The request body … Add your own `{provider}` key under Provider keys in the console to send it as it is. | Change the body as the message says, or add your own key. Limits: 8 MiB, whole within 60 s, plain JSON. See [Sizes](/reference/api#sizes). |
| `starter_credit_key_refused` | 502 | `{provider}` refused the starter credit's key, so this call was not served. Add your own `{provider}` key under Provider keys in the console to go on. | Add your own key for that provider. |
| `starter_credit_busy` | 429 | This project already has `{n}` calls in flight on the starter credit, its limit at once. Try again shortly, or add your own key under Provider keys in the console. | Wait the seconds in `retry-after`, or send fewer calls at once. |
| `starter_credit_unavailable` | 503 | The gateway could not use this project's starter credit just now. Try again shortly. | Wait the seconds in `retry-after`, then try again. |

### Path errors

| Code | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unknown_route` | 404 | Unknown route. … | Use a path under one of the [provider prefixes](/reference/api#paths). |
| `unknown_provider` | 404 | Unknown provider. The OpenAI-compatible providers this gateway serves at `/compat/<provider>/v1` are: … | Put one of the services the message lists in the `/compat` path. |
| `admin_path_refused` | 403 | Organization and admin endpoints are not available through this gateway. Call the provider directly. | Call your provider directly for organization and admin endpoints. |
| `invalid_path` | 400 | The request path has a `.` or `..` segment, a `;`, a control character, or an escape that decodes again. | Send the path your provider documents, as it is. |
| `no_provider_configured` | 503 | Says that this address makes no provider calls. Its type is `middleware_error`. | The call went to the console's address. Use the base URL your console's Connect page shows. |

### Connection and capacity errors

| Code | Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream_unreachable` | 502 | Could not connect to `{upstream}`. Nothing was sent. Try again shortly. | Try again shortly. |
| `upstream_failed` | 502 | The connection to `{upstream}` failed before it answered. | Your provider may have the request. Try again if a second call is safe for your app. |
| `upstream_redirect` | 502 | `{upstream}` answered with a redirect (HTTP `{status}`). … | Check the path against your provider's API. Mubit doesn't follow redirects, so a retry gets the same answer. |
| `upstream_timeout` | 504 | No answer from `{upstream}` within `{seconds}` s. | The provider didn't start its answer in time. For long answers, stream. |
| `gateway_overloaded` | 503 | This gateway is at its connection limit. Nothing was sent. Try again shortly. | Wait the seconds in `retry-after`, then try again. |
| `gateway_draining` | 503 | This gateway instance is shutting down. Nothing was sent. Try again. | Try again. Nothing was sent. |

## Your provider's errors

Mubit passes your provider's answers back to your app, its errors included.

An error whose type is `middleware_gateway_error` or `middleware_error` came from Mubit. An error without either, on an answer that carries `x-middleware-request-id`, came from your provider as it sent it. An answer without that header didn't come through Mubit's API: check the base URL and try again.

Your provider's message says why. The usual causes:

| Status | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 or 403 | Your provider refused the key. | An admin checks the provider's key under **Provider keys**. |
| 429 | Your provider account's limit was reached. | Check the limits on your provider account. |
| 400 | Your provider refused the request. | Read its message: it says why. |
| 404 | The model or path wasn't found. | Check the model ID, then send the call again. |
| 5xx | Your provider had a problem. | Try again shortly. |

| Problem | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Your Gemini calls fail, and your Gemini key is on the free tier. | Google doesn't serve its free tier in some countries. Use a paid-tier Gemini key. |

## Find a call's request ID

Each answer carries the call's ID in the `x-middleware-request-id` header. Mubit's own errors also carry it in their body. It starts with `mreq_`.

[Requests](/guides/requests#find-a-calls-request-id) shows how to read the header in Python, TypeScript and curl.

**Requests** shows its own ID for each call, under **Details**. It is not the request ID: see [Find a call's request ID](/guides/requests#find-a-calls-request-id).

## Get help

When you ask for help with a call, include:

- the call's request ID, from `x-middleware-request-id`;
- when you sent it, with your time zone;
- the status, the error's code and its message;
- the base URL and path, and the SDK you use, with its version.

Never send your Mubit key or a provider key.
